Samadhirajastura/Gilgit Manuscript
Chapter 1
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> / Gilgit Manuscript. Chapter 1.

children.text:
2461-1 /// + + + [mā]sakaṃpāsikābhiś ca | .. tkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjitaḥ ś ca ta
2461-2 /// + + sya vandanīyaḥ pūjanīyo namaskaraṇīya | tatra khalu bhagavān a
2461-3 /// % rṣada parivṛta puraskṛto dharmo deśayati sma | ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye
2461-4 /// svārthaṃ suvyaṃjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakā
2461-5 /// ḥ samayena tasminn eva parṣatsannipāte candraprabho nāma kumārabhūtaḥ
children.translated_text: [Folio 2461] ... [he was] honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and ... to be saluted, to be worshipped, to be bowed to. Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded and attended by [the assembly], taught the <s>Dharma</s> — good at the beginning, good in the middle, ... meaningful, well-phrased, complete, perfect, pure, and immaculate, proclaiming the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). ... At that time, in that very assembly, there was a prince named <s>Candraprabha</s>.

children.text:
2462-1 /// .. jinakṛtādhikāro varupitakuśalamūlo jātismaraḥ labdhapratibhāno mahāyānasaṃ
2462-2 /// tha khalu candraprabhakumārabhūtaḥ utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ prāvṛtva dakṣiṇaṃ jānu
2462-3 /// % na bhagavāṃs teṇāṃjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam etad avacat* pṛccheyam ahaṃ bha
2462-4 /// + + [b]uddhaṃ kaṃcid eva pradeśaṃ sacen me bhagavann avakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭapraśnavyākaraṇā
2462-5 /// + + + .ārabhūtam āmaṃtrayati sma | g.ccha tvaṃ kumāra tathāgatam arhantaṃ samya
children.translated_text: [Folio 2462] ... one whose roots of merit had been planted by former <s>Jinas</s>, who remembered his past births, who had attained eloquence, devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. ... Then the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>, rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee [on the ground], ... joining his palms and bowing to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'I would ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> ... the <s>Buddha</s>, a certain matter, if the <s>Bhagavān</s> would grant me the opportunity to have my question answered.' ... [The <s>Bhagavān</s>] addressed the prince: 'Go, O prince, [and ask] the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One.'

children.text:
2463-1 /// + + + .. tasyaiva praśnasya pṛṣṭasya vyākaraṇena cittam ārādhayiṣyāmi | sarvajño smi
2463-2 /// + + .[y]. ksaṃbuddha sarvadharmavalavaiśāra[d]ya .[ṛṣ]abhitām anuprāp[t]aḥ anāvaraṇavimokṣa
2463-3 /// % māra tathāgatasya sarvadharme svajñātaṃ vā adṛṣṭaṃ vā aśrutaṃ vā aciditaṃ vā
2463-4 /// [b]uddhaṃ va anantānaryantesu lokadhātuṣu nityakṛtas te kumārāvakāśo bhavatu ta
2463-5 /// .. | ahan te tasya tasyaiva [p]raśnasya pnaṣṭavyākaraṇena cittam ārādhayiṣyāmi | a
children.translated_text: [Folio 2463] ... 'By the answer to that very question asked, I shall delight [your] mind. I am omniscient, ... the Perfectly Awakened One, having attained the eminence of power and confidence in all <s>dharmas</s>, with unobstructed liberation. ... O prince, for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are either self-known, or unseen, or unheard, or unconsidered. ... the <s>Buddha</s> ... in infinite and boundless world-systems, always — may there be opportunity for you, O prince. ... I shall delight [your] mind by answering each question asked.'

children.text:
2464-1 /// ṣṭa udagra āttamanā pramudita prītisaumanasya jātaḥ stasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavantaṃ
2464-2 /// saṃbuddha lokanātha prabhaṃkaraḥ labhate cintiyaṃ jñānaṃ vyākuruṣva hitaṃkaraḥ || katha ca
2464-3 /// % naradevapūjanīya | atuliya varu labdham agrayānaṃ girivara priṣṭu vi
2464-4 /// + + .ch. mi śāṭhyaṃ mama na vidyate | sākṣī na kaścid anyo me anyatra puruṣottamāt* ||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2464] ... delighted, elated, joyful, cheerful, with gladness and happiness arisen, at that moment [addressed] the <s>Bhagavān</s>: ... 'O Perfectly Awakened One, Lord of the World, Light-maker, one obtains inconceivable knowledge — explain, O Benefactor! || How does ... worthy of worship by men and gods? Having obtained the supreme, incomparable vehicle, ... like a mountain peak, I wish to ask. ... there is no guile in me. There is no other witness for me except the Supreme Person. ||'

children.text: 2464-5 /// + + + .. jānasi mahya śākyasinhaḥ na ca ahu vacanavittako bhaviṣye laghupra
children.translated_text: [Folio 2464 cont.] '... you know me, O Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, and I shall not be one of deceitful words, swift-minded ...'

children.text:
2465-1 /// + + + [r]. kā dharmā buddhayāne bahūkarāḥ vyākurusva mahāvīra sarvadharmāṇa pāra
2465-2 /// + + .ā ya naru niṣevata bhoti tīkṣṇaprajñaḥ || apagatabhayabhairavo atrasto na ca
2465-3 /// % vyapagatamadarāgadoṣamohaś carati ca cārika sarvaśāntadoṣaḥ || kathaṃ na tya
2465-4 /// + kathaṃ niṣevate raṇyaṃ kathaṃ prajñāya vardhate ||| katha daśavalaśāsane udāre abhirati
2465-5 /// [bh]. vati acchidru śīlaskandha katha ca tuleti svabhāvu saṃskṛtasya || kathaṃ kāyena vānā
children.translated_text: [Folio 2465] '... what <s>dharmas</s> are most beneficial for the <s>Buddhayāna</s>? Explain, O Great Hero, the perfection of all <s>dharmas</s>. ... the person who cultivates [this] becomes one of sharp wisdom. || Free from fear and dread, unafraid, ... free from intoxication, passion, hatred, and delusion, he wanders on his journey with all faults pacified. || How does he not abandon ...? How does he resort to the forest? How does his wisdom grow? ||| How does he delight in the noble teaching of the Ten-Powered One? ... How does the aggregate of morality become unbroken? How does he comprehend the nature of conditioned things? || How by body and ...'

children.text:
2466-1 /// ṣṭaś ca cittena buddhajñānaṃ niṣevtate ||| katha bhavati viśuddhakāyakarmā katha ca vivarji
2466-2 /// [s]aṃkiliṣṭacitta puruṣavarā mama pṛṣṭu vyakurusvaḥ || atha khalu bhagavāṃś candrapra
2466-3 /// % kadharmeṇa kumāra samanvāgato bodhisatvo mahāsatva etān* guṇān* pra
2466-4 /// + .. m abhisaṃbudhyate | katamenaikadharmeṇa | iha kumāra bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ sa
2466-5 /// + + + apratihatacittaḥ aviṣamacittaḥ anena kumāraikadharmeṇa samanvāga
children.translated_text: [Folio 2466] '... and with his mind he cultivates the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. ||| How does his bodily action become pure? How does he abandon ... the defiled mind? O best of men, answer what I have asked. ||' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> [addressed] <s>Candraprabha</s>: ... 'By [possessing] one <s>dharma</s>, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> attains these qualities ... and awakens to [supreme enlightenment]. By what one <s>dharma</s>? Here, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> ... with an unobstructed mind, with an even mind — by this one <s>dharma</s>, O prince, being endowed,'

2467-2 /// + + .. dhyabhāṣataḥ || ekadharmaṃ samādāya bodhisatvo mahāsatva ya vartate | etān gu

2467-4 /// % yathāparikīrtitān viśesān* samaṃ cittaṃ niṣevitvā vipāko darśetaḥ samaḥ sama
2467-5 /// .. raḥ samaviṣamacittu bhāvayitvā apagatadoṣakhilaḥ prahīṇakāṃkṣaḥ caraṇavara
2467-6 /// .āsvaraśuddhadarśanīyāḥ daśadiśita viroci bodhisatvaḥ spharati śirīya | prabhāya
children.translated_text: [Folio 2467] '... obtains [these qualities] and swiftly awakens to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> ... spoke in verse: || 'A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who takes up this one <s>dharma</s> and abides [in it] — these qualities ... ||| His mind is never obstructed; one whose mind is unobstructed is a <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Nor is he ... Having cultivated an even mind toward the excellences as proclaimed, the result is shown: even, equal ... Having cultivated an equal and unequal mind, with faults and hindrances gone, with doubts abandoned, endowed with excellent conduct ... of pure and beautiful appearance, the <s>bodhisattva</s> shines forth in the ten directions, radiating with glory and light.'

children.text:
2468-1 /// .[i] tada aha satva sthapepi buddhajñāne ||| tatra kumāra sarvasatveṣu samacitto bodhisatvo hita
2468-2 /// sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatāvipaṃcitaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate | katamaś [c]a kumāra sarva
2468-3 /// % samādhiḥ yaduta kāyasaṃvaro vāksaṃvaro manaḥsaṃvaraḥ karmapāriśuddhiḥ āraṃvaṇasa
2468-4 /// % tā | āyatanā[p]akarṣaḥ tṛṣṇāprabhāṇaṃ | anutpādasākṣātkṛyāvatāraḥ hetudīpa
2468-5 /// + + [m]ārgabhāvanā | tathāgatasamavadhānaṃ | tīkṣṇaprajñatā | satyānupraveśajñānaṃ | dharma
2468-6 /// + + .. [bh]ed.jñānaṃ | vastūnāṃ samatik[r]. maḥ ghoṣaparijñā dhātusamatā | prāmodyaprati
children.translated_text: [Folio 2468] '... then I establish those beings in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. |||' 'There, O prince, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, with an even mind toward all beings, with benevolent [intent], ... attains the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>sarva-dharma-svabhāva-samatā-vipaṃcita</s> (Elucidation of the Equality of the Nature of All Dharmas). And what, O prince, is [this] ... <s>samādhi</s>? Namely: bodily restraint, verbal restraint, mental restraint, purification of <s>karma</s>, ... drawing back from the sense fields (<s>āyatanas</s>), abandoning of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), entering into the realization of non-arising, illumination of causes, ... cultivation of the path, agreement with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, sharpness of wisdom, knowledge of entering into the truths, <s>dharma</s> ..., knowledge of ..., transcendence of things, comprehension of sounds, equality of elements (<s>dhātus</s>), joy and ...'

children.translated_text: [Folio 2502-2503] ... for the benefit of beings, disgusted with the conditioned, he strides seven steps into the forest — thereby his merit becomes distinguished. || Having heard ... from the <s>Bhagavān Ghoṣadanta Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, these verses connected with renunciation of such a nature ... 'I understand the meaning. The <s>Bhagavān</s> does not praise the perfection of generosity (<s>dāna-pāramitā</s>). The <s>Bhagavān</s> praises something else — utter purity, utter ... ultimate conclusion, ultimate <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — the <s>Bhagavān</s> praises [this].' This thought arose in him: 'This is not easy ... to attain in its meaning. I have fallen away from the supreme practice of the <s>Dharma</s>. Let me shave off my hair and beard ... and go forth from home to homelessness.' Thus, O prince, King <s>Mahābala</s>, together with eighty thousand <s>brāhmaṇas</s> ... approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, and having approached, saluted the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet with his head ... [Folio 2503] ... <s>Mahābala</s>, having heard this <s>samādhi</s>, was delighted, elated, joyful, cheerful, with gladness and happiness arisen, and shaving his hair and beard ... went forth from home to homelessness out of faith. Having thus gone forth, he took up this <s>samādhi</s>, learned it, ... cultivated it, and being devoted to the practice of cultivation, he proclaimed it. By that very root of merit, for ten <s>kalpa-koṭis</s> (millions of aeons) ... he pleased [many] <s>Buddha-koṭīs</s>. During those ten <s>kalpa-koṭīs</s>, from all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> ... he heard this <s>samādhi</s> in succession, and having heard it from those <s>Buddhas</s>, he took it up, mastered it, ... and being devoted [to practice] he proclaimed it. Then, after a full thousand <s>kalpas</s>, he awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) ... the Perfectly Awakened One, and ... having accomplished the welfare of beings, he finally passed away with the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of a <s>Buddha</s> ... O prince.

2505-5 /// + + .. % rājasya tadekubhuṃ jate dvitīyucārdhasya abhūṣi rājā || mahābalasyo vijitasmi buddho utpannuso devamanu
2505-6 /// + [d]dh[ā]mupasthahīvarṣasahasrapūrṇam* tasyānuśikṣībahu anyisatvāḥ kurvaṃti satkāru tathāgatasya lokāmiṣeṇo na hi dha
2505-7 /// utsadaḥ || abhūṣi cittaṃ puruṣottamasya deśeṣyidharmaṃ ima dharmakāmāḥ ya nūna sarvave prajahitva kāmān iha prabraje
children.translated_text: [Folio 2505] ... this <s>samādhi</s> of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> conduces to the bringing about of unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. ... [The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:] 'I shall speak of the past. In an inconceivable <s>kalpa</s>, the supreme among men arose — a world-benefiting great sage, known by the name <s>Ghoṣa</s>...' ... 'The first [assembly] of <s>śrāvakas</s> was ...; the second was a full seventy [<s>koṭīs</s>]; the third was sixty <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>arhats</s>. || All of them ... had gone to the end. His lifespan was twenty-two thousand years, and his field was pure and beautiful. ||| In this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> there was ... a king. The <s>Buddha</s> arose in the realm of <s>Mahābala's</s> conquest, as a teacher of gods and men. ... For a full thousand years they attended ... the <s>Buddha</s>, and many other beings followed his training, making offerings to the <s>Tathāgata</s> with worldly gifts, but not with the <s>Dharma</s> ... The thought arose in the Supreme Person: "Let me teach the <s>Dharma</s>; these lovers of the <s>Dharma</s> — may they all abandon desires and go forth here.'

children.text: 2506-1 /// .. narāṇa[m]uttamasaṃlekhadharmaṃ sugatānas[i]kṣ[ān*] gṛhavāsadoṣāś ca anattaduḥkhā pratipatti dharmeṣv ayadharmapūjāḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2506] '... the supreme practice of renunciation for men, the training of the <s>Sugata</s>; the faults of household life and the suffering of the self; practice in the <s>dharmas</s>; and the worship of the <s>Dharma</s>. ||'

children.text:
2506-2 /// + .[t]eti rahogato nṛpaḥ na śakyu gehasmi sthihitva sarvā pratipadyituṃ uttamadharmapūjāḥ sa rā[j]u .yaktvā yatha khe[ṭ]. piṇ. aṃ pr[ā]
2506-3 /// + + + [m]ī tasya jinasya antikevanditva pādau purataḥ athito bhūt* teṣāṃ jino āśayu jānamāno deśetimāṃ samādhi durdṛ
2506-4 /// + + .. % dagrāstadaprabrajiṃsuḥ te prabrajitvāna imaṃ samādhiṃ dhāritva vācitva paryāpuṇitvāḥ na jātu gacchīvini
2506-5 /// + + + .. te tena sarve kuśalena karmaṇā adrākṣu buddhāna sahasrakoṭiyo | sarveṣu co teṣa jināna śāsane te pra
2506-6 /// + + + + + bhūṣibuddhā dṛḍhaśūranāmena anantaviryāḥ kṛtvā ca arthaṃ bahuprāṇakoṭināṃ te paścakāsmi śikhī
2506-7 /// + + + + + śūr[o] abhubuddhu loke | tadā hubahuprāṇasahasrakoṭiya sthapetva bodhāya sa paśca nivṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2506 cont.] '... thus [reflected] the king in solitude: "It is not possible, while remaining in the household, to fully practice the supreme worship of the <s>Dharma</s>." That king, abandoning [his realm] like ... spittle, ... approached that <s>Jina</s>, saluted his feet, and stood before him. The <s>Jina</s>, knowing his disposition, taught this <s>samādhi</s>, difficult to [master] ... they were elated and went forth. Having gone forth, they retained, recited, and mastered this <s>samādhi</s>. Never did they go to the lower realms ... By that wholesome <s>karma</s>, they all beheld thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. | And in the teaching of all those <s>Jinas</s>, they ... became <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Dṛḍhaśūra</s>, of infinite vigor, and having accomplished the welfare of many <s>koṭīs</s> of beings, they finally [attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>] as <s>Śikhin</s> ... the Hero arose as a <s>Buddha</s> in the world. Then many thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of beings were established in awakening, and thereafter he passed away. ||'

children.text: 2507-1 /// + + + + [bu]ddhavarṇitaṃ | dhāritvimaṃ īdṛśa dharmakośaṃ bhavisyase buddhunarāṇam uttamāḥ || %% ||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2507] '... praised by the <s>Buddha</s>. | Having retained this treasury of <s>Dharma</s> of such a kind, you shall become <s>Buddhas</s>, supreme among men. || %% ||'

Chapter 6
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> / Gilgit Manuscript. Chapter 6.

children.text:
2507-1 /// tasmāt tahi kumāra bodhisa
2507-2 /// + + + + .. parikarmaḥ karaṇīyaṃ | tatra kataraḥ samādhiparikarmaḥ iha kumāra bodhisatvo mahāsatvo mahā
2507-3 /// + + .. [t]ānāṃ parinirvṛtānāṃ vā pūjākarmaṇe udyukto bhavati | yaduta cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglāna pratyayabhai
2507-4 /// + + pa % nacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākābhiḥ stūryatāḍāvacarai tac ca kuśalamūlaṃ samādhipratilaṃbhāya pari
2507-5 /// .. .[t]. [th]āgataṃ pūjuyati | na rūpaṃ na kāmān na bhogān na svargaṃ na parivāra | na sarvatraidhātuke vyavacāraniḥ sṛtaḥ api tu kha
2507-6 /// .. rmakāyato pi tathāgataṃ na manupaśyati | nopalabhate | kim aṃgapunar anyaṃ dharmakāyata upalasyate | tasmāt tarhi ku
2507-7 /// [y]aduta tathāgatasyādarśanamānaś cānupalabdhiḥ karmavipākasya cāpratikāṃkṣaṇatā | anayā tṛmaṇḍalapariśu
children.translated_text: [Folio 2507 cont.] 'Therefore, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva</s> ... should undertake the preparation for <s>samādhi</s>. What is the preparation for <s>samādhi</s>? Here, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> ... is devoted to the worship of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, whether living or passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — namely, with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick ... incense, powder, robes, parasols, banners, and flags, with musical instruments and dances. And that root of merit he dedicates to the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> ... He worships the <s>Tathāgata</s> — not for form, not for desires, not for enjoyments, not for heaven, not for retinue, not for any experience in the three realms. Rather ... from the <s>Dharmakāya</s> also he does not perceive the <s>Tathāgata</s>, does not apprehend [him]. How much less anything else apart from the <s>Dharmakāya</s>? Therefore, O prince, ... namely, not perceiving the <s>Tathāgata</s> and not apprehending [him], and not expecting karmic fruition — by this threefold purification of the <s>maṇḍala</s> ...'

children.text:
2508-1 /// + samādhiṃ pratilabhate | so nena[tṛ]maṇḍalapariśuddhena pariṇāmenakiyaparī .tanāpi puṣumamālyaga[n]dhavilepanena ta[th]ā
2508-2 /// .. riṇamayati | tasya tat kuśalamūlam acintyaṃ bhavatyaci .yavipākaṃ | imaṃ ca samādhiṃ pratilabhate | kṣipraṃ .. .. [rā]ṃ samyak[s]aṃ[bodh]i
2508-3 /// + + .. mā gāthā abhāṣataḥ || anantajñānisyadadi[t]vā ga .dhā ana[n]tu gandho bhavatī navāṇām* | kalpānakpṭīya brajanti durga .. .. ..
2508-4 /// + + [ri]kāṃ % pūjitva[b]uddhāna sahasrakoṭyaḥ te jñātva gandhena samudgatena bhavaṃti buddhā .. ra .īlagandhikāḥ || sa[c]e[t p]una .. ..
2508-5 /// + + + % tena cintena cadātigandham eṣāsya kṣāntirmṛdukānulomikīḥ || tasyaita kṣāntī adhimātru sevataḥ [s]a .e ..
2508-6 /// + + + .. na tasya cittaṃ bhavatīvivartiyaṃ ||| kiṃ kāraṇaṃ vuccati kṣānti nāma kathaṃ puno vuccati ānulomi .ī | [a] .. .. .. [ko] ..
2508-7 /// + + + + + [sm]i ddharme prakṛtīnirā .ma[k]e nairātmyasaṃjñisya kileśunāsti | khaṃ yādṛśaṃ jānati sa[r]vadharm[ā]ṃs tasmādihā
children.translated_text: [Folio 2508] ... obtains samādhi. By this threefold purification of the maṇḍala, with the transformation [...] and also with flowers, garlands, fragrance, and ointments, thus [...] | [...] he suffuses [all beings]. His root of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) becomes inconceivable, of inconceivable fruition. And he obtains this <s>samādhi</s>; quickly [...] unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) [...] | [...] spoke these verses: || 'Having given [to one of] infinite knowledge, the fragrance [...] the fragrance becomes infinite for the Nine. For <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> they go to [...] | [...] having worshipped thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, they, knowing by that supreme fragrance, become <s>Buddhas</s> [...] of virtuous fragrance. || If again [...] | [...] with that thought, transcending fragrance always — this is his patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), gentle and conforming (<s>anulomikī</s>). || Of one who cultivates this patience intensely [...] | [...] his mind becomes irreversible (<s>avivartya</s>). ||| Why is it called patience (<s>kṣānti</s>)? And why again is it called conforming (<s>ānulomikī</s>)? [...] | [...] in this <s>dharma</s> whose nature is peaceful, for one who has the perception of selflessness (<s>nairātmya-saṃjñā</s>), defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) do not exist. Just as space — so he knows all <s>dharmas</s>; therefore here [...]'

children.text:
2509-1 /// + + + + + kṣat. na cāsya dharmaṃ caratevicakṣaṇaḥ .. .. ddhadhar[m]. ṣujaneti saṃśayān iyāṃ sa kṣāntī bhavatānulomakā | evaṃ ca
2509-2 /// + + + + + .. sudurlabhābodhivarāhi śrāvako na gṛhṇatīvākyuna co jvartate | bodheti satvān viṣamātu dṛṣṭito na eṣa mā
2509-3 /// + + .. % peti | taṃ kāraṇaṃ ucyati bodhisatvaḥ || kṣamisya nūloma pathe sthitasya nairātmyasaṃjñāya vibodhitasya | svakṣāntare py a
2509-4 /// + .v.ḥ || % sacimārakoṭyo yathagaṃgabālukās te buddharūpeṇa upāgamitvāḥ bhaneyur abhayantarakāyijīv[o] te
2509-5 /// .. jānāmy ahu skandhaśunyatā jñātvā ca kleśehi na saṃvasimi | vyavahāramātreṇa ca vyoharāmi parinirvṛto lomaṃ carāmi |||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2509] '... [...] he does not cause harm. And the discerning one does not practice the <s>dharma</s> [for himself] [...] he removes doubts in [...] beings — this patience becomes conforming (<s>anulomakā</s>). | Thus [...] | [...] the supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is extremely difficult to obtain; the <s>śrāvaka</s> does not grasp it and is not [thereby] afflicted. He awakens beings from wrong views — this is not [...] | [...] for that reason he is called a <s>bodhisattva</s>. || For one of patient endurance, standing on the conforming path, awakened to the perception of selflessness (<s>nairātmya-saṃjñā</s>), within his own patience [...] | [...] || Even if <s>Māra</s>-<s>koṭīs</s> as numerous as the sands of the Ganges were to approach him in the form of <s>Buddhas</s>, saying: "There is a self (<s>ātman</s>), a soul (<s>jīva</s>)" — those [...] | [...] I know — I understand the emptiness of the aggregates (<s>skandha-śūnyatā</s>), and knowing this, I do not associate with the defilements (<s>kleśas</s>). I speak only by way of convention (<s>vyavahāra-mātra</s>); [though] completely liberated (<s>parinirvṛta</s>), I conduct myself [in the world]. |||'

children.text:
2509-6 /// [t]. mināmā ayam eva nāmaḥ nāmaṃ [n]a tasya diṣatā sulabhyate tathāsya nāmaṃ na kutaścid āgataṃ | tathaiva nāmaṃ kṛ
2509-7 /// su labhyate | paryeṣamāṇo ayu bodhisatvo jānāti yo eva sa bodhisatvaḥ samudramadhye pi jyaleta agni
children.translated_text: [Folio 2509 cont.] '... this [is merely] a name — this very name; a name cannot be found as [truly] given. Likewise, his name has not come from anywhere; likewise, a name is [merely] constructed [...] | [...] is not [truly] found. The <s>bodhisattva</s>, seeking thus, knows — and he who knows thus is [truly] a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Even in the midst of the ocean, fire could blaze [...]'

children.text:
2510-1 /// tosya bodhāyaupannucittamatrāntare tasya na jīvadṛṣṭiḥ .. hy atra jāto na mṛto va kaś cid uta[p]anna satvo manujo naro vā | māyopa
2510-2 /// .tīrthikehi ||| na cāpi āhāradhimūrcchit* hi lubdhehi gṛddhehi capātracīvare | na coddhatehī na pi connaḍehi [ś]akyā iyaṃ jāni
2510-3 /// + īdai stabdhehi mānīhi anotramehi | teṣāna buddhasmi prasādu asti na śakya tehī varaḥ bodhijānitum* || na bhinna
2510-4 /// + .. sā % du astiḥ sabrahmacārīṣu ca nāsti goravaṃ na śakya tehī iya bhodhi budhyitum* || abhinna .ṛttā hiri
2510-5 /// + + .. ḥ % sabrahmacārīṣu ca tīvragauravaṃ prāpuṇaṃtī varabodhim uttamāṃ || smṛter upasthāni ha yeṣa gocaraḥ
2510-6 /// + + + + .. ru samādhi paniyaṃ budhyaṃti te hī vara bodhim uttamān* || nairātmyasaṃjñā ca [d]ivāhāro anusmatīcaṃ
2510-7 /// + + + + .. mā te yujyamānā varabodhi prāp[u]ṇī | yā bodhisatvānā carī cidrūnāṃ mabhūmir atyasya janasya ta
children.translated_text: [Folio 2510] '... for one whose mind has arisen toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), within this [very moment], there is no view of a self (<s>jīva-dṛṣṭi</s>). [...] For here nothing is born, nor does anything die — [no] being, person, or man has [truly] arisen. Like an illusion [...] | [...] by non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthikas</s>). ||| Nor [is this attainable] by those attached to food, nor by the greedy and covetous for robes and bowl; nor by the restless, nor by the arrogant — this knowledge [...] | [...] by the rigid, the proud, and the insolent. They have no faith in the <s>Buddha</s>; by them the supreme <s>bodhi</s> cannot be known. || Not by those of broken [...] | [...] conduct — they [...] have no reverence for fellow practitioners (<s>sabrahmacārins</s>); by them this <s>bodhi</s> cannot be awakened to. || Those of unbroken conduct, possessing shame (<s>hrī</s>) [...] | [...] and intense reverence for fellow practitioners — they attain the supreme, excellent <s>bodhi</s>. || For those whose domain is the establishment of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) [...] | [...] excellent <s>samādhi</s> to be aspired to — they indeed awaken to the supreme, excellent <s>bodhi</s>. || The perception of selflessness (<s>nairātmya-saṃjñā</s>) and [...] always mindfully [...] | [...] they, being engaged [in practice], attain the supreme <s>bodhi</s>. || Whatever conduct of <s>bodhisattvas</s> there is, of those [...] the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) beyond this person [...]'

children.text:
2511-1 /// + + + + + + cchandaḥ || sacen mamā āśuyu bhaveta etakaṃ kalpāna koṭyo yatha gaṃga bālikā | ekasya romasya bhaṇe ya varṇaṃ baudhe
2511-2 /// + + + + + .. nābhibhūtenaj inena deśitām* imaṃ samādhiṃ laghu uddiśeyā na durlabhābheṣyati agrabodhiḥ || %% ||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2511] '... [...] in meter (<s>chandas</s>). || If I were to have such an aspiration for <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and were to describe the qualities of a single hair — the <s>Buddha</s>-[qualities ...] | [...] [taught by] the unconquered <s>Jina</s>. If one were to quickly point out this <s>samādhi</s>, supreme awakening (<s>agrabodhi</s>) will not be difficult to attain. || %% ||'

2511-2 tasmāt tarhi ku
2511-3 /// + + + + .ā[m]āna tṛkṣānti kuśalena bhavitavyaṃ | tena prathamākṣāntiḥ prajñātavyāḥ dvitīyākṣātiḥ prajñātavyāḥ tṛtīyākṣāntiḥ prajñā
2511-4 /// + + .. jñā % nakuśalena ca bhavitavyam* tat kasya hetoḥ tathāhi kumāra yadā bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ kṣāntiviśeṣakuśalo bha
2511-5 /// + ayaṃ ku % māra bodhisatvo mahāsatva kṣipram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyate | tasmāt tarhi kumāra bodhi[sa]tvena mahāsa
2511-6 /// + + [m]. [n]āyaṃ tṛkṣāntyavatāro dharmaparyāya udgrahītavyaḥ udgṛhya ca parebhyo vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ tat bhaviṣyati bahujanahi
2511-7 /// + yair mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca | atha khalu bhagavāṃś candra[p]rabhasya kumārabhū
2511-8 /// [g]āthābhigītena saṃprakāṣuyati sma ||| na kena cit sādhu .aroti vigrahaṃ na bhāṣate camanarthasaṃhitaṃ arthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca sa
children.translated_text: [Folio 2511 cont.] Therefore, O prince, [...] one should be skilled in the three patiences (<s>tṛkṣānti</s>), skilled in wholesome [qualities]. The first patience is to be understood, the second patience is to be understood, the third patience is to be understood [...] | [...] one should be skilled in knowledge and in wholesome [qualities]. For what reason? Because, O prince, when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> becomes skilled in the special qualities of patience [...] | [...] O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> quickly awakens to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> [...] | [...] this <s>dharma</s>-discourse (<s>dharmaparyāya</s>) on the entrance into the three patiences (<s>tṛkṣāntyavatāra</s>) should be taken up; and having taken it up, it should be proclaimed to others in detail. That will be for the benefit of many people [...] | [...] for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. Then indeed the <s>Bhagavān</s>, [addressing] prince <s>Candraprabha</s> [...] | [...] illuminated [the teaching] with verses: ||| 'With no one does he engage in quarrel; he does not speak what is connected with harm. He [speaks of] meaning and <s>dharma</s> [...]'

children.text:
2512-1 /// śīyati || māyopaṃājānati sarvadharmān na cāpi so bhoti nimittagocara | na hīyate jñāna vivṛddhibhūya prathamāya kṣāntīya
2512-2 /// [v]ida subhāṣiminn adhimukta paṇḍitaḥ anantajñānī sugatāna jñāne prathamā kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ || yaṃ kaṃ cid dharama śṛ
2512-3 /// + + ti | adhimucyate sarvajināna dharmatāṃ prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viseṣāḥ || nītārthasūtrāntaviśeṣa jānatī yathopa
2512-4 /// + .. a % nyusatvo neyārthatāṃ jānati sarvadharmān* || ye asmi lpke pṛthu anyatīrthyā na tasya teṣu pratihanyate manaḥ
2512-5 /// + + .. % ime viśeṣāḥ || ābhāsam āgacchati tasya dhāraṇī tasmiṃś ca ābhāṣi na jātu kāṃkṣati | satyānuparivarti
2512-6 /// + + + .. ḥ || catūrṇa dhātūna siyā nyathātvaṃ vāyvaṃvutejaḥpṛthivīya cāpi | na co vivarteta sa buddhabodhe prathamāya kṣā
2512-7 /// + + + + .e sarveṣu co śikṣitu bodhisatvaḥ na cātmano uttavi kaṃ ci paśyati prathamāya kṣāntīya ime viśeṣāḥ || akaṃpi
children.translated_text: [Folio 2512] '... he trains. || He knows all <s>dharmas</s> as illusion-like, and he does not become one who grasps at signs (<s>nimitta</s>); his knowledge does not diminish but increases further — these are the special qualities of the first patience (<s>prathamā kṣānti</s>) [...] | [...] wise, well-spoken, devoted, learned — [endowed with] infinite knowledge in the knowledge of the <s>Sugatas</s> — these are the special qualities of the first patience. || Whatever <s>dharma</s> he hears [...] | [...] he is devoted to the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) — these are the special qualities of the first patience. || He knows the special [meaning of] <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>), as they are taught [...] | [...] the being who knows the provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>. || Those who are the many non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthyas</s>) in this world — his mind is not troubled by them [...] | [...] these are the special qualities [of the first patience]. || <s>Dhāraṇī</s> (retentive power) dawns upon him, and in that [power] he never doubts. He follows truth [...] | [...] || Even if the four elements (<s>dhātus</s>) were to change their nature — wind, water, fire, and earth — he would not waver from <s>Buddha</s>-enlightenment (<s>bodhi</s>) — [these are the special qualities] of the first patience [...] | [...] and the <s>bodhisattva</s> trains in all [matters], yet does not see any self as supreme — these are the special qualities of the first patience. || Unshakable [...]'

children.text:

children.translated_text: [Folio 2522] [...] he is called [thus] | he is called 'son of the <s>Buddha</s>' (<s>buddhaputra</s>) | he is called 'son of <s>Śākya</s>' (<s>śākyaputra</s>) | he is called 'one who has crushed the thorns' (<s>marditakaṇṭaka</s>) | he is called 'one who has raised the moat' (<s>ukṣiptaparikha</s>) | he is called 'one who has crossed the moat' (<s>tīrṇaparikha</s>) [...] he is called 'free from fever' (<s>nirjvara</s>) | he is called '<s>bhikṣu</s>' (mendicant) | he is called 'unobstructed' | he is called 'a man' (<s>puruṣa</s>) | he is called 'a true man' (<s>satpuruṣa</s>) [...] he is called 'lion among men' (<s>puruṣasiṃha</s>) | he is called 'man-given' (<s>puruṣadatta</s>) [...] | he is called 'elephant among men' (<s>puruṣanāga</s>) [...] | he is called 'thoroughbred among men' (<s>puruṣājāneya</s>) | he is called 'pure-bred among men' (<s>puruṣadhauveya</s>) [...] | he is called 'flower among men' (<s>puruṣapuṣpa</s>) | he is called 'lotus among men' (<s>puruṣapadma</s>) | he is called 'white lotus among men' (<s>puruṣapuṇḍarīka</s>) | he is called 'tamer of men' (<s>puruṣadamaka</s>) [...] he is called 'unstained among men' (<s>puruṣānupalīpta</s>) | Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that time spoke these verses: || "Just as in the world [...] just as before, so too after — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || This entire world, whatever exists, below and above, these aggregates [...] || Just as in the sky there are no clouds [...] yet by [...] a mass of clouds appears | knowing its former origin — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile!

2523-7 /// .. le na vinavidyate | tal lakṣaṇāṃ jānatha sarvadharman* || yathā naraḥ śailavanāntare sthitaḥ bhaṇeyya gāyeyya haseya
children.translated_text: [Folio 2523] [...] one sees a reflection in a mirror | just as before, so too after — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || Just as the great [...] of a river, without essence — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile as a path! || When the <s>devas</s> rain down with thick drops, various bubbles arise separately | having arisen [...] know all <s>dharmas</s> [by such a simile]! || Just as in a village a painting is seen, and actions are produced separately, both auspicious and inauspicious — there is no transfer of words to the painting [...] || [...] intoxicated with pride, wandering beings perceive the earth, yet the ground neither moves nor trembles — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || [...] A woman gazes [into a mirror], seeing her adorned face | she, the foolish one, generating passion there, is led astray, seeking desire || When there is no transfer of the face [...] || Just as a deluded one would generate passion — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || Just as the moon, pure in the sky, [is reflected] in a pure lake,

children.translated_text: [Folio 2524] [...] know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || In singing and playing of instruments, and likewise in weeping, an echo arises dependently | yet the substance of a voice is never found there — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || [...] In a dream one enjoys pleasures, [but] upon awakening the person does not see [them] | That fool, attached to desires, greatly desirous — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || [...] various chariots, horses, and wonderful things — yet no one is there as appears to be seen — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || Just as a young maiden in a dream, she [...] a son [...] || [...] in a state of distress — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || Just as the moon is seen in a water vessel, in clear, undisturbed water | [...] know all <s>dharmas</s> [by such a simile]! || Just as in the heat of summer at midday, a person parched with thirst goes forth and sees a mirage [as water] || [...] yet in the mirage there is no water — that deluded being wishes to drink it | There is no happiness in drinking unreal water — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || [...] one would split open a plantain trunk — outside and inside there is no essence — know all <s>dharmas</s> by such a simile! || Not by the eye [is <s>dharma</s> perceived]

children.translated_text: [Folio 2525] [...] If the sense faculties were a [valid] measure, what would be accomplished by the <s>āryamārga</s> (Noble Path)? ||| Since these sense faculties are not a [valid] measure, dull by nature, [...] one should accomplish the noble [goal] through the <s>āryamārga</s>! || When examining the prior end of the body, there is neither a body here nor a perceiver of body | where there is no body [...] it is declared [thus] ||| For one whose nature is cessation (<s>nirvṛtti</s>), there are no <s>dharmas</s> — by which 'it does not exist' [is said], those never truly exist | 'It exists' and 'it does not exist' — this is for those engaged in conceptual construction [...] || 'It does not exist,' 'both' — these are extremes | 'purity' — these too are extremes | Therefore, having abandoned both extremes, a wise one (<s>paṇḍita</s>) does not take a stand even in the middle ||

children.translated_text: [Folio 2525 cont.] [...] 'Pure' and 'impure' — this is a dispute | For those engaged in dispute, suffering does not cease | For those not engaged in dispute, suffering is extinguished ||| [Regarding] <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness), when a discourse is spoken [...] for one who is a witness of the body, there is [...] | When that is abandoned, all other [views] are [abandoned] || Having spoken a discourse on the four [<s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>], the foolish declare [...] they are not within the range [of understanding] | [...] through knowledge, intoxication is abandoned ||| Having spoken a discourse on the four [foundations], the foolish declare 'We are seers of truth' — yet for a seer of truth, there is no [such] conceit

children.translated_text: [Folio 2526] ... morality (<s>śīla</s>), and I do not consider that [sufficient] — one should hear the <s>Dharma</s>, and I do not consider that [sufficient either]. | By whatever he, the one of little wisdom (<s>alpaprajña</s>), thinks — that root of suffering increases for him. ||| The root of suffering [...] | Through pride (<s>mada</s>), suffering increases for the intoxicated one; for the one not proud, suffering ceases. || However much <s>Dharma</s> one would learn, one would not guard morality, intoxicated by learning [...] [...] by which, going to a bad destination (<s>durgati</s>). || If again he, intoxicated by morality through pride, does not apply himself to great learning (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>), having lost that portion of morality [...] [...] would understand <s>samādhi</s> in the world, nor would he understand the perception of self (<s>ātmasaṃjñā</s>). The defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) again become agitated, just as [...] in the absence of <s>samādhi</s> [...] [...] should examine whether he cultivates | Not [merely] for the attainment of the fruit of <s>nirvāṇa</s>; one who [pursues] another cause does not attain peace (<s>śānti</s>). || Just as a person [...] [...] sick, his feet are unable to walk; being seized there, he is killed. ||| Thus a person without morality, deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>), attempting to be strong [...] [...] to run swiftly, is killed by disease and death. ||| Just as among thieves, many thousands, with various means commit evil | Thus the defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) ...

children.translated_text: [Folio 2527] ... [...] those well-established, selfless in the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), when abused and reviled, do not become dismayed. | He does not fall under the power of the mind of defilements, who [understands] emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) [...] [...] emptiness, and does not understand that [things] are without self (<s>nirātmaka</s>). Those not understanding, urged by others, overcome by anger (<s>krodha</s>), speak harshly. || Just as a person who is ill [...] [...] is said to be afflicted with a long illness, tormented by suffering, seeks a physician, desiring a healer. || [...] [...] having been prescribed: 'Take this medicine and consume it!' || Having taken the medicine abundantly over time, the illness of the patient [...] does not [...] [...] at the proper time — it is not the fault of the physician nor of the medicines; it is the fault of that patient himself. ||| Thus here, having gone forth for peace [...] [...] they are devoted [to practice]. For <s>yogīs</s> not engaged in <s>yoga</s>, whence is there peace (<s>nirvṛti</s>)? All <s>dharmas</s> are empty by nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnya</s>); the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> perceive things as real [...] all [...] [...] of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers). ||| The wise do not quarrel with the foolish; respecting the lowly, they admonish. Where has one gone with corrupt mind? Not the foolish ...

children.translated_text: [Folio 2528] ... [...] having known the nature of fools in their continuity (<s>saṃtati</s>) — for however long fools are served, they become like enemies before [one]. | The wise [...] [...] the nature of <s>dharmas</s> — different by their own character (<s>svabhāva</s>). For ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) there is no [true] friendship. || Addressed with words of fellow <s>Dharma</s>-practitioners, [they respond with] anger and faults [...] [...] having understood this meaning of the <s>dharmas</s>, they do not trust. || The foolish do not meet the foolish on equal terms, just as filth [mixes] with filth. The wise, however [...] [...] || [...] without examining the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>: the ripening of <s>karma</s> is not understood; lacking faith in the words of the <s>Buddhas</s>, [they are] those who should be taught but cannot be instructed [...] [...] they are skilled in the arts and crafts; the impoverished have no wealth — making a livelihood, they go forth. || Having gone forth, here [...] [...] seized by evil companions, they do not heed the training of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One). || They do not observe their own morality [...] [...] and they do not desist from [...] evil <s>karma</s>. || With body and mind unrestrained, there is nothing that should not be uttered; always they seek the faults of others ...

children.translated_text: [Folio 2529] ... [...] they become guardians [of the rule], yet there is no moderation in eating. Having obtained food through the merit of the <s>Buddha</s>, those fools are ungrateful. || They [...] [...] are not engaged in <s>yoga</s>; for them, food becomes [a cause of] destruction, just as for vessels, poison unwashed — even though the wise, mindful, and discerning one [...] [...] is present there, the <s>yogī</s> eats without greed. || Even though the learned, mindful, and discerning one addresses the fool: 'Why, welcome!' [...] [...] he ascends and establishes [himself] there. | He who is compassionate toward fools and the harmful — satisfied with the fault of that [...] | By this fault [...] [...] in the forest. Having known such faults as mine, the wise one never associates with fools [...] [...] those of inferior wisdom who attend upon me — alas, the heavenly [...] [...] they become wise ones, dwelling in compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), dwelling in sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) | Equanimous (<s>upekṣaka</s>) always in all existences, having cultivated <s>samādhi</s>, they touch awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). || Those [who have attained] awakening [...] [...] having established compassion there, they discourse on what is connected with the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>). || Those who understand the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> ...

From <s>Āṭakāvatī</s>, the assembled royal city, <s>Guṇya</s> [...] [...] one after another, they all approach to see the Protector of the World. || And further, <s>Kharakarṇa</s>, <s>Sūciloma</s>, <s>Āṭavaka</s>, and likewise the <s>yakṣa Bhaiṣaka</s>, <s>Hemava[ta]</s>, [...] [...] worshipping the <s>Jina</s>, the Self-born One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>). || Those of deformed, ill-shaped bodies, misshapen and of many hideous forms — many hundreds of thousands at that time [...] [...] The <s>Suparṇas</s> (Garuḍas) who dwell in the ocean waters approach having assumed the guise of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, wearing diadems, wondrous in appearance, stationed in the sky [...] [...] and certain deities in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in forest groves — all the deities of the city, assembled together, approach to perform worship for the Leader. |||

children.translated_text: [Folio 2539] [...] in the excellent [assembly] they perform wondrous displays. || They indeed make offerings of praise to the excellent <s>Jina</s> (Victor), entering the supreme city in [the presence of] the Guide. || <s>Devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s> [...] | [...] In former births, the Lord of the World (<s>Lokanātha</s>) performed supreme worship for former <s>Jinas</s>; such is the fruit and ripening (<s>vipāka</s>) of merit (<s>puṇya</s>) — not [even] a king, a lord of men [...] | [...] <s>Himavat</s> (the Himālaya) and likewise <s>Gandhamādana</s>; those coverings of his become radiant when the <s>Jina</s> releases [light] in the <s>Buddha</s>-field. ||| And whatever oceans [...] | [...] become; the entire surrounding <s>Buddha</s>-field becomes strewn with flowers. ||| Immeasurable hundreds of thousands of rays [...] | [...] the hells become cool, suffering is removed and [beings] experience happiness. ||| The <s>Dharma</s> is proclaimed by the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten-Powered One) there; the eye of gods and humans becomes purified. ||

2540-7 /// + + + + + + [y]amotvāru vadāhināyakaḥ kathaṃ jātismaru bhoti nāya kānacāpi garbhe upapadyate kathaṃ | kathaṃ parīvāru
children.translated_text: [Folio 2540] Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, entering into the residential street of prince <s>Candraprabha</s>, [...] the prince <s>Candraprabha's</s> [...] and having entered, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then prince <s>Candraprabha</s>, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>bhikṣus</s>, was seated, [...] with exquisite and abundant hard food, soft food, lickable food, drinkable food, and water, he served the <s>Bhagavān</s> to satisfaction; and when the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished eating, [...] with hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> [...] of pairs of garments, he covered the <s>Bhagavān</s>; and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṅgha</s> [...] || Then prince <s>Candraprabha</s>, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having placed his right knee on the ground, [bowing to] the <s>Bhagavān</s> [...] having bowed down [...] he questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses: ||| 'How should the wise <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct himself, always knowing the true nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of <s>dharmas</s> [...] | [...] speak, O Guide (<s>Nāyaka</s>)! How does one become a rememberer of past births (<s>jātismara</s>)? In whatever womb he is born, how [...] | [...] retinue [...]'

2541-7 /// m anantā kathaṃ carantaś carimottaraṃti | carīpraveśaṃ mama deśaya svayaṃ śrutva satvāna cariṃ prajāniyāṃ || vilakṣaṇaṃ dharmasva
children.translated_text: [Folio 2541] '[...] You know the conduct of all beings; in all <s>dharmas</s>, your knowledge operates; unvanquished, O Supreme Among Bipeds (<s>dvipadānām uttama</s>), I ask you a question [...] | [...] you know the [...] nature; you proclaim the inexpressible. As jackals are not bold before a lion, so too are other <s>tīrthikas</s> (sectarians) before the <s>Buddha</s>. || All [...] | [...] your knowledge operates unobstructedly. With unobstructed knowledge and purified domain — prophesy for me, O Lord of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmasvāmin</s>)! || You know the past and likewise the future; whatever [...] | [...] knowledge operates unobstructedly — therefore I ask [you] here, O Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s> (<s>Śākyasiṃha</s>). ||| The <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of the <s>Jinas</s> joined to the three times — you know that <s>dharmatā</s>, O <s>Dharma</s> [...] | [...] therefore I ask [you] here, O Ocean of Knowledge (<s>Jñānasāgara</s>). ||| Whatever <s>dharma</s> there is, nothing is faulty in it; therefore the mind is entirely abandoned. Free from all knots and delusion [...] | [...] || Whatever characterless <s>dharma</s> has been awakened to by the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) — that characterized <s>dharma</s>, reveal to me! Having understood that characterized <s>dharma</s>, I shall practice that characterized awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) [...] | [...] immeasurable — how, by practicing, does one cross over to the final goal? Reveal to me the entry into the practice; having heard, may [all] beings understand the practice. || The characterless <s>dharma</s> [...]'

children.translated_text: [Folio 2542] '[...] isolated and directly perceived — how do <s>bodhisattvas</s> [attain this]? Reveal to me the <s>Buddha</s>-eye (<s>buddhanetrī</s>)! || In all <s>dharmas</s>, having gone to the farther shore of perfection (<s>pāramī</s>), in all instructions [...] | [...] cutter of doubts — reveal to me the <s>Buddha</s>-awakening (<s>buddhabodhi</s>)!' || Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing with his own mind the mental deliberation of prince <s>Candraprabha</s> [...] | [...] spoke thus: 'By one <s>dharma</s>, O prince, having arrived at equality (<s>samatva</s>), a <s>bodhisattva</s> obtains these qualities and quickly awakens to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) [...] | [...] O prince, how does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> know the true nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> as it truly is? And how, O prince, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> [know] all [...] | [...] the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> knows all <s>dharmas</s> as nameless, formless, devoid [of self-nature]; devoid of speech, beyond the path of words, beyond syllables [...] | [...] characterless, beyond conditions, beyond the character of [karmic] ripening, beyond the character of [...] isolation, of one character, namely, the character of [...] | [...] gone beyond — [the <s>bodhisattva</s>] knows all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. || Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, [spoke] these <s>gāthās</s> (verses) [...]

2543-7 /// [k]. [ṭ]īyo saṃsaraṃte punaḥ punaḥ || sacet te kalpa jānīyur yathā jānāt[i] nāyakaḥ na teṣ. ṃ duḥkhajāyeta nāpi ga
children.translated_text: [Folio 2543] '[...] characterless, taught by the supremely wise one who knows as it truly is. ||| Whichever <s>bodhisattva</s> understands this teaching of <s>Dharma</s>, for him there is no [...] | [...] he knows the ultimate point (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>). And he knows that point, yet nothing is expressed therein. ||| By one [dharma] he knows all; by all he sees the one. However much [...] | [...] thus his mind is absorbed: all <s>dharmas</s> are nameless. Trained in the instruction of names, he speaks true words. || He hears whatever sound [there is]; the past [...] | [...] he is not carried away by that sound. || Just as [one knows] a person's past, so too is the characterless nature of <s>dharmas</s>. Understanding <s>dharmas</s> thus, one is not born in wombs [...] | [...] he knows non-arising. Understanding the instruction on birth, he becomes [...] of birth [...] || When he becomes a rememberer of past lives (<s>jātismara</s>), then he practices action; action upon action [...] | [...] the <s>bodhisattva</s> who thus knows <s>dharmas</s> as empty — for him nothing remains unknown; this ultimate point is without anything whatsoever. ||| Whatever ultimate point is without anything [...] | [...] they transmigrate again and again. || If they were to know <s>kalpas</s> as the Guide (<s>Nāyaka</s>) knows them, for them suffering would not arise, nor would they go [...]'

2544-7 /// + + + + .. ntiyo bhoti varṇo na śakyu paryantu kṣametu tasya ||| yaḥ śunyatāṃ jānati bodhisatva karoti sarthaṃ bahuprāṇako
children.translated_text: [Folio 2544] [...] All those who are ignorant of this method reject such <s>dharmas</s> wherein suffering is extinguished ||| One who is ignorant of all <s>dharmas</s> operates with the perception of <s>dharma</s> | that [...] know this! The perception of consciousness is conceptualized by the deluded — in unconceptualized <s>dharmas</s>, the wise (<s>paṇḍitas</s>) are not confused ||| This is the ground of the wise [...] the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of <s>dharmas</s> — <s>dharmas</s> are unstained || This is the ground of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, this is the practice of sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, this ornament of <s>Buddha-dharma</s> has been taught as peaceful and pure [...] their habitual tendencies are [exhausted] — they are not carried away by form, they are established in the <s>buddhagotra</s> (lineage of the Buddha) ||| All <s>dharmas</s> are without [fixed] abode — this ground is not found [...] difficult to obtain || Having cultivated <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>śruta</s> (learning), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), and the excellent friends (<s>amitrabhadraka</s>), understanding this practice, one quickly awakens to <s>bodhi</s> ||| <s>Devas</s> and <s>nāgas</s> [...] <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, [...] <s>rākṣasas</s> and night-wanderers — all pay homage to him || His fame [...] and <s>buddhakoṭis</s> (millions of Buddhas) praise him abundantly [...] his virtues cannot be measured to the end ||| The <s>bodhisattva</s> who knows <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) acts as a caravan leader for many living beings

2545-5 /// + [ya] yujyate | virocamānena samucchuyeṇa dvātṛṃśa kāye sya bhavaṃti lakṣaṇā anyānanantān bahu ānuśaṃsān bodhiṃ ca so ca

2545-7 /// ṣu careyya paṇḍitaḥ || mitra sa bhotī sada sarvaprāṇināṃ yo bodhicittas midṛḍhaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ na cāndhakāra sya kadāci bhoti
children.translated_text: [Folio 2545] [...] they generate reverence for him ||| And their knowledge expands vastly — thereby they behold the supreme among men, the <s>Jina</s> | and they see in the [Buddha]-fields the arrays [...] || Know all <s>dharmas</s> as illusion-like — just as [...] examining a magical creation as empty, one understands the nature of those magical creations — thus practicing [...] accomplishes the purpose | dwelling in the excellent <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of awakening) || Having examined all <s>dharmas</s> through knowledge, they send emanations (<s>nirmita</s>) to other [Buddha]-fields, performing <s>buddhakṛtya</s> (the work of a Buddha) [...] they go according to the nature of reality (<s>dharmatā</s>) || They accomplish their purpose as they intend — those who are established in <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) without abiding in [...] | He becomes [a friend] of the <s>Buddhas</s> [...] | With a radiant and exalted [body], thirty-two <s>lakṣaṇas</s> (marks) appear on his body, and other infinite and abundant benefits — and he [attains] <s>bodhi</s> [...] ever unshakeable, kings [...] his majesty | he becomes gracious, of great consecration, endowed with merit, splendor, and glory [...] even the <s>devas</s> cannot [...] || The wise one should practice in [...] || He becomes a friend to all living beings always — one whose <s>bodhicitta</s> is firmly established | and darkness never befalls him

children.translated_text: [Folio 2546] [...] Gone beyond speech and words, inexpressible, the path of <s>dharmas</s> is like space, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is the inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s> — knowing this supreme state, then [...] speaking hundreds of thousands [of teachings], with subtle wisdom [...] former [lives], he always becomes a knower with unobstructed speech, understanding the subtle inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s> [...] he becomes skilled in manifold sounds and expressions | and the discernment of the fruits of <s>karma</s> — [these are] distinguished and eminent qualities of such a kind || With complete [...] the wise one, the great self — his <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is always perfectly pure, knowing the subtle inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s> || He does not hear what is unpleasant [...] his speech is always pleasant, knowing the subtle inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s> || Endowed with <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), <s>mati</s> (intellect), <s>gati</s> (attainment), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) [...] he expounds hundreds [of teachings], in manifold ways, knowing the subtle inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s> || Skilled in the analysis of syllables and words, he knows many expressions [...] knowing the qualities of the nature of <s>dharmas</s> || For <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and <s>kinnaras</s> — always, for them he

children.translated_text: [Folio 2548] [...] the eldest sons of the powerful one — they have worshipped many <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) for a long time || I too have seen here on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), and what was done by me then, they too were [...] of the <s>Buddha</s> [...] and there will be a prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) at that time ||| And further, the <s>Buddha</s> there speaks to them of the lifespan, teaching many benefits — all these [...] behold the <s>Buddha</s> supreme! || For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, the danger of downfall never occurs | for one who practices this excellent <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of awakening) [...] || Therefore this is most excellent of such a kind — these supreme benefits have been proclaimed | practicing and training step by step under me [...]||

children.translated_text: [Folio 2552] [...] the <s>Buddha</s>, endowed with great qualities, having trained here, becomes skilled, bearer of the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), he becomes a <s>Buddha</s> || Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> again [addressed] <s>Candraprabha</s> (Moonlight) [...] therefore, O <s>Kumāra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should be skilled in <s>samādhi</s>. Now, O <s>Kumāra</s>, what is the exposition of <s>samādhi</s>? It is [...] equality (<s>samatā</s>) | non-conceptualization (<s>akalpanā</s>) | freedom from false conceptualization (<s>avikalpanā</s>) | non-distortion (<s>aviḍhapanā</s>) | non-arising (<s>asamutthānatā</s>) | non-production [...] | non-cessation (<s>anirodhatā</s>) | [...] cutting off the mental support of consciousness (<s>cittārambaṇa</s>), non-attention (<s>amanasikāra</s>), cutting off of representation (<s>vijñaptisamuccheda</s>), cutting off of discursive thought and conceptualization (<s>vitarkavikalpasamuccheda</s>), cutting off of attachment, aversion, and delusion (<s>rāgadoṣamoha</s>) [...] cutting off of [unwholesome] attention, knowledge of the inherent nature of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases (<s>skandhadhātvāyatanasvabhāvajñāna</s>) | [endowed with] <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>mati</s> (intellect) [...] the domain of conduct and practice [...] | the ground of non-conflict (<s>araṇābhūmi</s>), the ground of peace (<s>śāntabhūmi</s>), the cutting off of all conceptual proliferation (<s>sarvaprapañcasamuccheda</s>), all the trainings of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the domain of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>

children.translated_text: [Folio 2553] [...] this, O <s>Kumāra</s>, is called the exposition of <s>samādhi</s>. A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> established in this exposition of <s>samādhi</s> is never separated from [...] endowed with <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), and serves the welfare of all immeasurable beings | Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that time [spoke] these verses: [...] this ground is peaceful, subtle, and very difficult to see — the <s>samādhi</s> that uproots all perceptions is therefore so called ||| Non-conceptualizing and free from false conceptualization, ungraspable, and [...] — the <s>samādhi</s> is therefore so called ||| When one is concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>), one does not conceptualize any <s>dharmas</s> — non-conceptualization as it truly is, this is proclaimed as <s>samādhi</s> || [...] is not found — the <s>samādhi</s> of non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s> is therefore so called ||| And the non-apprehension of mind — this too is called conceptualization — those <s>dharmas</s> are unconceptualized — the <s>samādhi</s> [...] the object and that word are without substance, sound is like an echo, like the sky, like space — these <s>dharmas</s> are indeed unestablished, and their establishment is not obtainable [...] is not obtained by [...] | 'It passes away' and 'it comes' — such a course (<s>gati</s>) is not found — courselessness expressed by the word 'course' — this is <s>samādhi</s> from the standpoint of course || Not concentrated

children.translated_text: [Folio 2554] ... this is the second conceit (<s>manyanā</s>). | Without conceit they wander toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>); the one without conceit touches supreme awakening. || Equal, without inequality — this peaceful [...] [...] this sign having been cultivated, this peaceful <s>Buddha</s>-lineage (<s>buddhagotra</s>) — he here is engaged in the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> (<s>samādhibhāvanā</s>). And this cannot again be expressed in syllables [...] [...] having abandoned all sounds and the practice of speech, he becomes concentrated, and there is no conceit in him. ||| And whatever <s>bodhisattva</s> [practices] this <s>samādhi</s> as instructed [...] [...] they say without false conceptualization — in the <s>Buddha</s>-field, like a mountain stronghold, it is not [consumed] by fire. || Just as space has never been burned before, even by many aeon-thunderbolts [...] [...] those <s>dharmas</s>, therefore he is never [destroyed] in the midst of fire. || And if again, in a blazing <s>Buddha</s>-field, he makes a vow, having been established in <s>samādhi</s>, the blaze [...] [...] there is no alteration. || His supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) and strength become infinite; he travels like a bird, unattached. These qualities [...] [...] having been established. || He knows [when he] passes away, and there is neither birth nor death; for him who has this understanding, this <s>samādhi</s> is not difficult to obtain. ||

children.translated_text: [Folio 2555] ... [...] world-protectors [...] having thus known the <s>samādhi</s>, by that [...] unstained by worldly <s>dharmas</s> [...] [...] he always sees in [...] the Perfectly Awakened Ones, the Leaders of the World (<s>lokanāyaka</s>); and there he hears the <s>Dharma</s> proclaimed by the <s>Buddhas</s> in their fields. ||| His [...] ignorance is not [...] [...] always in the <s>Dharma</s>, for he is one who follows the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). || Though he speaks for <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, his eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>) does not diminish. He creates [...] by the hundreds [...] [...] they go, created by the <s>bodhisattva</s>, seated cross-legged on thousand-petaled lotuses. || They illuminate <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, [endowed with] <s>dhāraṇī</s> [...] [...] this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> should be cultivated. || They establish many inconceivable beings in non-retrogression (<s>avaivartika</s>). Their eloquence does not diminish [...] awakening [...] [...] they [...] | They scatter [the <s>Vināyaka</s> (Guide)] with jewel-adorned [offerings] and with fragrant flowers. || They scatter with fragrant powders [...] the Guide [...] [...] for the sake of awakening. || These qualities of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the protectors, are immeasurable. When they become free of defilements (<s>niṣkleśa</s>), then they obtain supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) ...

That which is difficult to know and [expressed] through sound — by that this <s>samādhi</s> is proclaimed. ||| Inexhaustible [...] [...] of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) without concealment. || The definite training of all <s>Buddhas</s> is the two-nature-lessness of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dvabhāvatā</s>). Having trained [...] Perfectly Awakened [...] [...] the far shore or [...] the prior limit is not conceptualized; therefore all those <s>Buddhas</s> have gone to the perfection of qualities ...

children.translated_text: [Folio 2576] ... he obtains this <s>samādhi</s>. By which four [qualities], O prince, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> become gentle (<s>sūrata</s>)? [He is] tamed through pleasant association, having attained the stage of the tamed (<s>dāntabhūmi</s>). When reviled or abused by others, he is patient with those who act wrongly, those who cause harm, and those on the path of fabrication — being of a nature that practices forbearance (<s>adhivāsana</s>). He sees [the results of] <s>karma</s>, has cast down pride, and loves the <s>Dharma</s>. By this first quality, O prince, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having attained equanimity in the <s>Dharma</s>, obtains this <s>samādhi</s>. || Furthermore, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is endowed with morality (<s>śīlavān</s>) — of completely purified morality, unbroken morality, unimpaired morality, [...] unstained morality, unfallen morality, unturbid morality, blameless morality, transcendent morality, [...] free from clinging morality [...] | [...] morality praised by the wise. By this second quality, O prince, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having attained equanimity in the <s>Dharma</s>, obtains this <s>samādhi</s> [...] | [...] the <s>mahāsattva</s> becomes one whose mind is fearful regarding the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>) — with a frightened mind, a disgusted mind, a mind seeking escape, without desire, without delight, [...] | [...] with an anxious mind: 'Except for [beings in] the three realms, I shall liberate all those who are suffering' — thus he resolves. There arises unsurpassed [...]

children.translated_text: [Folio 2580] '... skilled in discerning speech, grammar, and etymology, having become [true] ornaments, they wander over the earth. || For the benefit of all beings they conduct their wandering — the great and powerful sons of the <s>Sugata</s>. children.translated_text: [Folio 2585] [...] always [...] and the knowledge of entering into sounds, with meaning ascertained through etymological analysis, grammatical form, and context — always avoiding all that is harmful — thus the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) taught the <s>dharma</s>, the master || [...] the conduct [...] of cowardly men is such | Always [maintain] faith (<s>prasāda</s>) and love toward the <s>Jina</s> | thus the <s>Jina</s> taught the supreme <s>dharma</s> || And cessation through dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) [...] and among the peaceful [...] non-attachment even toward gain — thus the <s>Jina</s> taught the highest <s>dharma</s> || Having obtained honor, one should not be astonished; even when dishonored, one should remain equanimous — [...] never [...] such is the teaching for the welfare of the world || One should endure abuse and slander completely, along with praise, together with all householders | one should not [...] with those who have gone forth — thus the <s>Jina</s> taught, the master of <s>dharma</s> || Established in the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, having abandoned all that is outside the domain, perfect in conduct, with well-tamed mind — this <s>dharmanetrī</s> (guidance of <s>dharma</s>) was taught by the <s>Sugata</s> || One should abandon foolish <s>dharmas</s>, and should avoid all that corrupts the family — the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching must always be protected — thus the <s>Jina</s> taught, the master of <s>dharma</s> || One should speak little, well-connected, and with benevolence, with gentle words to others ||| For those seeking benefit, the restraint of the <s>saddharma</s> (true teaching) — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind ||| One should confess [faults] at the proper time and at the improper time, one should not trust all ordinary people | touched by suffering, one should not become dejected — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> [...] having seen [...] one should make efforts; the immoral should be viewed [...] to be instructed

children.translated_text: [Folio 2586] One should always speak for the sake of what is beneficial — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind || One should guide beings through <s>dharma</s> [...] renouncing worldly bait, and one should [...] | one should not accumulate [...] — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind || Praise of good conduct and censure of bad conduct, non-deceitfulness, and cultivation of moral discipline — not being attached to all possessions and wealth — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind ||| With a superior intention, unreservedly devoted to the teacher — as one speaks, so should one act in all things | one should constantly attend upon the preacher of <s>dharma</s> — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind ||| One should always be respectful, with a joyful mind, always established in a gentle outlook, always well-resolved in former practices — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind || Always foremost in wholesome practices, in the abandonment of signs through skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), in the reversal of perceptions, and in the characteristics of things — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind || Skill in the expositions of <s>sūtras</s>, and the practice of training in the knowledge of liberation — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind [...] one should always cultivate <s>dharmas</s> of awakening, being confident, established in the power of moral discipline, one should surpass through the mastery of <s>samādhi</s> — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind || One should never [...] gain through relatives [...] and should not [...] for others | one should abandon all that is based on [wrong] views — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind ||| Supreme in eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>), in excellent <s>dhāraṇī</s>, in the radiance of knowledge, with infinite [...] skill in eloquence — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind ||| One for whom there is no door [closed] — such a one is a knower of the path; the practice of instruction and guidance is excellent

children.translated_text: [Folio 2587] [...] instructions [...] this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind [...] the <s>anulomikī kṣānti</s> (conformity patience) which was described by the <s>Buddha</s> — established in patience, one should abandon faults | avoiding the ignorant, established in knowledge — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> [...] || Established in knowledge, and adorned with proclamation, the practice of <s>yoga</s> for those set on awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), constant association with true persons (<s>satpuruṣa</s>) — [this is] the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind || The improper [...] is to be avoided; the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (ground of the Buddha) spoken by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, investigated by learned <s>paṇḍitas</s> — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind || Protected and guarded by [...] of the ignorant, not being the ground of those of limited learning, but embraced by <s>bodhisattvas</s> — this is the instruction of the <s>Jina</s> of such a kind ||| This was realized by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, honored and worshipped by <s>devas</s> | rejoiced in by thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Brahmās</s> — at some point the <s>Jina</s> teaches this <s>samādhi</s> || Always well-honored by thousands of <s>nāgas</s>, by <s>suparṇas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and by humans | the supreme awakening spoken by the <s>Jinas</s> — at some point the <s>Jina</s> teaches this <s>samādhi</s> || That which is mastered by the truly wise, the foremost and excellent wealth well-obtained, free from material taint, the supreme medicine of knowledge — at some point the <s>Jina</s> teaches this <s>samādhi</s> || The treasury of knowledge, inexhaustible eloquence, and this is but a portion of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>sūtras</s> — full comprehension of the three realms, true knowledge — at some point the <s>Jina</s> teaches this <s>samādhi</s> || A raft [...] for those going to the far shore, a ship for those crossing the flood | fame and glory increase, a garland of renown, for those to whom this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> has been taught || This is praised [...] by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> [...]

children.translated_text: [Folio 2588] [...] for the excellent among men | the qualities of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and the method [...] by whom this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> has been taught || This is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), the illumination for the pacification of faults, the ground of [...] arising [...] | [...] of those of great fame, for whose sake this <s>samādhi</s> was spoken || This practice has been taught as the lion's roar (<s>siṃhanāda</s>), the approach to the supreme, immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge | the seal of the inherent nature (<s>svabhāvamudrā</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> — this <s>samādhi</s> was taught by the guides (<s>nāyakas</s>) || And the vehicle of omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñāna</s>), this is the practice for those set on awakening | and the terrifying of <s>Māra</s>'s hosts — this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> was taught by the <s>Jina</s>, as the approach to supreme <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, the seals of the inherent nature of all <s>dharmas</s> [...] the seal of <s>dharma</s> that is unconditioned — this <s>samādhi</s> was taught by the guide || This is the science (<s>vidyā</s>) of those established in <s>dharma</s>, and the supreme protection amidst enemies [...] the <s>samādhi</s> that restrains adversaries — this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> was taught by the <s>Jina</s>. The ground of eloquence (<s>pratibhānabhūmi</s>) has been illuminated, the powers (<s>balas</s>), liberations (<s>vimokṣas</s>), and likewise the faculties (<s>indriyas</s>) ||| The eighteen distinguished <s>buddhadharmas</s> — this <s>samādhi</s> should be cultivated [...] || The investigation of the ten powers in their true nature, and the prior signs of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge | the <s>buddhadharmas</s> proclaimed by the best of men, illuminated for the welfare of the world || [...] the path was taught for those desiring liberation | and the delight of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> therein — hear this peaceful <s>samādhi</s>, hard to see! || That which is the fulfillment of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge [...] the wise one seeks [...] this peaceful <s>samādhi</s> || One whose body is purified like that of the <s>Jinas</s> — liberation-knowledge and liberation-vision | without

children.translated_text: [Folio 2595] ... [...] having held this <s>samādhi</s>. || He will stand before the foremost World-Protector, of beautiful, long-[enduring] marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and minor marks (<s>vyañjana</s>). | And there will be no one who steals his knowledge, having held this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>. [...] [...] his thought will never be [...] he will be wealthy, not poor. | And his mind will not become agitated, having held this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>. || And he will not remain in unfavorable conditions — a sovereign, he will become a wheel-turning king (<s>cakravartin</s>). | Always his kingdom will be secure, having held this supreme, peaceful <s>samādhi</s>. || His knowledge will be vast — of this there is no doubt — for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> while speaking [...] having heard this [<s>samādhi</s>] ...

children.translated_text: [Folio 2596] ... who cultivates the supreme qualities of austerity, having been established in practice, he will hear this <s>sūtra</s>. ||| Not from the hand of an evil-doer will this <s>sūtra</s> be heard; not by those whose morality (<s>śīla</s>) has been corrupted in the presence of the World-Protectors (<s>Lokanātha</s>). | For the heroic celibate practitioners (<s>brahmacārin</s>), whose thought is unagitated — those who are supported by the <s>Buddhas</s> — from their hands it will be heard. | Those former <s>Buddhas</s>, the World-Protectors, who attended — from their hands this <s>sūtra</s> will be heard in the future age. ||| But those who in former births were <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) — for them, having heard this <s>sūtrānta</s>, there will be no delight. ||| And those who, having gone forth here in my teaching for the sake of livelihood, corrupted by gain and honor (<s>lābhasatkāra</s>), they despise one another ...

children.translated_text: [Folio 2597] '... accomplished by me in [the pursuit of] awakening among others. || Having placed his golden hand upon the crown [of his head], the Teacher, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, spoke to <s>Candraprabha</s>: "I make this empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) for you, O prince [...] | [...] in the future [...] the <s>brahmacarya</s> (holy life) [...] and his will be." ||| Others too, eight [...] arose elsewhere as holders of the <s>Dharma</s>: "We too, in the future age, shall be holders of this <s>sūtra</s>." || Gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s> [...] | [...] eighty <s>koṭīs</s> assembled, and another sixty <s>nayutas</s> addressed the Leader of the World: || "We, for these <s>bhikṣus</s> who have now arisen — in that future age, we shall provide protection, O Guide!" || [...] | [...] by [the power of] this <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>-fields were shaken, as many as the sands of the Ganges, by the empowerment of the Teacher. || And those fields that were shaken — in all of them <s>Buddha</s>-emanations were sent for the benefit of the world, and <s>dharmas</s> were illuminated. || And from each field, inconceivable <s>koṭīs</s> of beings, having heard this <s>Dharma</s>, were established in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. || And from these <s>Buddha</s>-fields, ninety <s>koṭīs</s> [...] | [...] having generated the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), showered the <s>Buddha</s> with flowers. || They were prophesied by the Lord of Men — in eighty <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, all in a single <s>kalpa</s> shall become Guides. || <s>Bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, and <s>upāsikās</s> — six successive <s>koṭīs</s> of beings by whom this <s>sūtra</s> was heard — they too were prophesied by the <s>Buddha</s>: they shall see the Leaders of the World. As many as the sands of the Ganges, walking the path of awakening [...] | [...] they shall worship all those established in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. There they shall hear this <s>sūtra</s> without impediment — in eighty <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> they shall become Leaders of the World [...] all in a single <s>kalpa</s>, compassionate [...]'

2598-1 nukaṃpaka || maitreyasya ca buddhasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā niruttarāṃ | saddhadharmaśreṣṭhadhāritvā gamiṣyaṃti sukhāvatim* || yatrāsau virajo buddho amitāyus tathāgataḥ tasya pūjā kariṣyaṃ

children.translated_text: [Folio 2598] '... having performed unsurpassed worship of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, and having upheld the supreme true <s>Dharma</s>, they shall go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Land of Bliss). || Where that stainless <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> (of Infinite Life), [dwells] — they shall make worship of him for the sake of supreme awakening (<s>agrabodhi</s>). || For seventy-three incalculable [future] <s>kalpas</s>, they shall not go to lower realms of misfortune, having heard this supreme <s>sūtra</s>. || Whoever in the future age shall hear this supreme <s>sūtra</s>, they shall shed tears [of devotion] — by all of them am I [truly] honored. || I proclaim to all who stand before me: I entrust this awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) which was attained by me through hardship. || %% ||'

children.translated_text: [Folio 2598 cont.] Therefore, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who aspires to this <s>samādhi</s> should be skilled in the exposition of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; he should be one who is born of asking about the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; he should be one devoted to the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; he should be skilled in the investigation of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. ||| Having heard the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, one should not be frightened, should not be terrified, should not fall into terror. || When this was said, prince <s>Candraprabha</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'How then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> become skilled in the exposition of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and skilled in asking about the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? And how is he devoted to the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? And how [...] | [...] does he become skilled in the investigation of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? And having heard the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, how does he not become frightened, not become terrified, not fall into terror?' ||| At that time, a <s>gandharva</s>-prince (celestial musician) named <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, together with five hundred [...] | [...] was in attendance upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the <s>gandharva</s>-prince, had this thought: 'Just as for the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) heaven, <s>Śakra</s> [...]'
