2599-8 kika devamunuṣyā nopi sa saṃkaru no ca utsataḍākā ||| nāpi ca saṃkaru no ca upīḍā evam acintiyu dharmajinānāṃ | tatra padehi ca parvata nekā cakravāda api meru
children.translated_text: [Folio 2599] '... of <s>Indra</s>, in [the hall of] <s>Sudharmā</s> [...] | [...] performs attendance and service, and I set music playing — just so, today, for the God above gods (<s>devātideva</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, let me set music playing as worship.' || Then <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the <s>gandharva</s>-prince, together with those five hundred instruments and those five groups of <s>gandharva</s>-princes, with music and songs united in a single harmony, taking up the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) of <s>Vaindraryataṇḍā</s>, played before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. || Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> had this thought: 'Let me create such a supernatural transformation (<s>ṛddhyabhisaṃskāra</s>) by which prince <s>Candraprabha</s> may attain skill in the contemplation of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and may obtain the <s>samādhi</s> which discerns the equality of the nature of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmasvabhāvasamatā</s>); and let me teach <s>Pañcaśikha</s> the skill of the triple melodic voice.' || Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> created such a supernatural transformation. ||| From those five hundred instruments, being played together, a sound issued forth, infused with compassion, connected with the <s>Dharma</s>, and these verses contemplating the inconceivable <s>dharmas</s> resounded by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>: ||| 'On a single hair-tip [there are] many <s>Buddhas</s> — as many as the sands of the river Ganges; and just as many are the fields of those <s>Jinas</s>. And they are distinct, they are dissimilar. || The beings born in the five destinies on [that] hair-tip — those in the hells, those in the animal realm, those in <s>Yama</s>'s world, the gods and humans — there is no confusion among them, nor any crowding. |||'

children.translated_text: [Folio 2600] '... Nor is there confusion, nor oppression — such is the inconceivable <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>. || There on [that] point are also many mountains — <s>Cakravāḍa</s>, <s>Meru</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Mucilinda</s>, great <s>Mucilinda</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), and <s>Himavān</s> (the Himalayas). ||| There on [that] point are hells — <s>Tapana</s> (Scorching), <s>Pratāpana</s> (Great Scorching), <s>Anabhiramya</s> (Joyless); and those beings born in those hells experience painful sensations and suffering. ||| There on [that] point are also divine palaces, twelve <s>yojanas</s> [in extent], delightful; in them are many thousands of <s>Maruts</s> (wind-gods) enjoying divine pleasures and happiness. ||| There on [that] point is also the arising of <s>Buddhas</s> — the Teacher, the Knower of the World, shines forth. He who has not purified his conduct does not see him, but one whose conduct is purified and cleansed [sees him]. || There on [that] point the <s>Dharma</s> also ceases; the Guide is heard to have attained <s>nirvṛti</s> (liberation). || There on [that] point too, some hear and believe that the Guide speaks the <s>Dharma</s>. || There on [that] point too, for some, lifespans of inconceivable years — thus is their perception. ||| There on [that] point too, some experience [only] a moment, and soon the sound "arisen and passed away" [is heard]. || There on [that] point too, some have the perception of having seen the <s>Tathāgata</s> and worshipped the <s>Buddha</s> — delighted in mind, with the perception of faith; yet they have neither worshipped nor been reborn [there]. Like a person dreaming in his own house, experiencing pleasure in sense-objects, he, upon awakening, does not see the sense-pleasures, and he understands: "That was a dream." || Likewise, what is seen, heard, sensed, and known — all this is like a dream. Whoever gains this <s>samādhi</s>, he knows the nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of <s>dharmas</s>. || Those who are well-established [...] in the world, for whom there is neither pleasant nor unpleasant [...] | [...] terrified in caves, they find supreme happiness in the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇaka</s>). || Those for whom "mine" does not exist anywhere, those who are free from fatigue [...] | [...] they wander through the world like space, they travel through the sky. ||| The path is cultivated, knowledge set in motion; all <s>dharmas</s> are followed as empty, without self [...]'

children.text:
Samadhirajastura/Gilgit Manuscript
Chapter 20
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> / Gilgit Manuscript. Chapter 20.

children.text:
2601-1 ra bodhisatvena mahāsatcena sarvakuśalamūlaśn[p]āguṇadharmaniśitena bhavitavyaṃ | saṃsargabahulena cabhavitavyaṃ | pāpamitraparivarja[ka]na | kalyāṇamitrasa
2601-2 nniśritena | pa[r]ipṛccha[ṃ] kajātīyena dharmaparyeṣ[ky]āmatṛptena prāmodyabahulena dharmarthikenā dharmakāmena | dharmaratena | dharmapariśrāhakena | dharmanudharmapratipannena
2601-3 śāstṛsaṃjñā[t]ānena sarvabodhisatveṣūtpāda[dhāra]tavyāḥ yasya cāntikād imaṃ darmaparyāyaṃś caṇovi tena tasyānti ketīcraṃ goravaṃ śāstrisaṃjñā cotpādayitavyāḥ yaḥ kumā
2601-4 ra bodhisatvo mahāsatva imān dharmāt samādāya va % rtante sa kṣipramanācchedyapratibhānaniryāto bhavati | acintyabuddhadharmādhimuktaś ca bhavati gaṃbhīreṣu va dha
2601-5 rmeṣu nidhyaptiṃ gacchati | ālokabhūtaś ca bhavati sadekasya lokasya kāṃkṣāvimativicikit[s]āndhakāravidhamanatayā atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyā
2601-6 m imā gāṃprā abhāṣataḥ || abhyatīya vahukaṇpakoṭiy anuprameya atulā avittiyā | yada abhūṣi dupadān anuttamo indraketudh[vu]rāju
2601-7 nayakaḥ || so mā + + + + .. .. deśayi yatra nāsti naru jīva pudgalaḥ māya budbuda marīcividyu cā sarvadharma dagacandra sanpibhāḥ || haṣti
children.translated_text: [Folio 2601] ... a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should be sharpened in all wholesome roots (<s>kuśala-mūla</s>), qualities, and <s>dharmas</s>. He should be abundant in association [with the good], avoiding evil friends (<s>pāpa-mitra</s>), relying on spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇa-mitra</s>), of an inquiring nature, insatiable in seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, full of joy (<s>prāmodya</s>), desiring the <s>Dharma</s>, loving the <s>Dharma</s>, delighting in the <s>Dharma</s>, grasping the <s>Dharma</s>, practicing in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>, perceiving [the teacher] as the Teacher (<s>śāstṛ-saṃjñā</s>) — toward all <s>bodhisattvas</s> [this perception] should be generated. And toward the one from whom one hears this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, one should generate respect, reverence, and the perception of the Teacher. O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who takes up and abides in these <s>dharmas</s> quickly attains inexhaustible eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>). He becomes one of faith in the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and gains contemplative insight (<s>nidhyapti</s>) into the profound <s>dharmas</s>. He becomes a light for this world, by dispelling the darkness of doubt, uncertainty, and hesitation. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that time spoke these verses: || 'Having passed incalculable, immeasurable, incomparable, inconceivable <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, when there arose the Unsurpassed among Bipeds, the leader <s>Indraketu</s> [...] || He taught me where there is no person (<s>nara</s>), no soul (<s>jīva</s>), no individual (<s>pudgala</s>) — [all dharmas are like] illusion (<s>māyā</s>), bubbles (<s>budbuda</s>), mirages (<s>marīci</s>), and lightning (<s>vidyu</s>); all <s>dharmas</s> are like the moon reflected in water. || [Like] an elephant...

children.text:
2602-1 rtta manujo va labhy. .. + .. .. tva paralokigacchi yoḥ no ca karmakṛtu vipraṇaśyate kṛṣṇa śukla halu deti tādṛśaṃ ||| eṣa yuktinayudvāra bhadrakaṃ
2602-2 sūk. sa dra .[ṛś]. jināna gotaraḥ yatra akṣarapadaṃ na abhyate buddhabodhi bhagavān* prajānati || dhāraṇī vipulajñānasaṃcayo sūtrakoṭinayu ..āna ā
2602-3 gaṃ[m]. .. ddhakoṭinayutāna gocaras ya samā % dhi bhagavān* prabhāṣate ||| āturāṇamaya vyādhimocako bodhisaṃtva samudānitaṃ dhanaṃ | sarvabuddha
2602-4 stuna saṃpraharṣito devakoṭinayutehi pū % jito | sarvavālajana bhūtacodanā tīrthikehi parivarjitaḥ sadā śreṣṭhaśīladhanu buddha .. ṇitaṃ |
2602-5 vidyutāva gagane na lipyate | yehi pūjita jināna koṭiyo dānaśīlavaritā cakṣaṇā || pāpamitra puri yehi vajitā tesa paitṛkadhanaṃ ni
2602-6 ruttaraṃ | tatra bhikṣu sthitu dharmabhāṇako brahmavāri mugatasya auraso | śrutvā dharmapimamānulom[i]kaṃ cintupādusi ya lokanāyakaḥ | indra
children.translated_text: [Folio 2602] ... a human [birth] is obtained [...] going to the other world — karma once done does not perish; black and white [karma] yields such [results]. ||| This is the proper method, the excellent entrance — the subtle lineage (<s>gotra</s>) of the <s>Jinas</s>, where the imperishable syllable-word is not grasped — the <s>Bhagavān</s> knows <s>Buddha</s>-awakening (<s>buddha-bodhi</s>). || <s>Dhāraṇī</s>, the accumulation of vast knowledge, <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>sūtras</s> [...] [...] the domain of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> — such is the <s>samādhi</s> the <s>Bhagavān</s> proclaims. ||| The healer of the sick, the treasure accumulated by the <s>bodhisattva</s>, rejoiced in by the praises of all <s>Buddhas</s>, worshipped by <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>devas</s>, the inspirer of all foolish beings, always avoided by <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers), having the bow of supreme morality (<s>śīla</s>), the <s>Buddha</s> [...]

children.text:
2603-1 ketudhvajarāju nāyako adhyabhāṣi amu dharmabhāṇakam* bhikṣuparamaṃ ti d[ra]ṣkaraṃ cintu pādu [v]a[ra a]śra bodhay[e] | śīlu rakṣa maṇiratnasannibhaṃ
2603-2 mitra meca ṣada ānulomikām* pāpamitra ma kadāci sevato buddhajñānumacireṇa lapsyase |||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2603] ... the leader whose banner and standard are supreme, addressed this <s>Dharma</s>-preacher (<s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>): 'Difficult to see is this supreme <s>bhikṣu</s>; guard the thought and the noble [aspiration for] awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). || Guard morality (<s>śīla</s>) like a jewel (<s>maṇi-ratna</s>); seek the friend who is appropriate and conforming. Never associate with evil friends (<s>pāpa-mitra</s>) — you will quickly obtain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.' |||

children.text:
Samadhirajastura/Gilgit Manuscript
Chapter 21
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> / Gilgit Manuscript. Chapter 21.

children.text:
2603-2 āsi pūrvam iha jaṃbusāhvaye apramatta duviśreṣya
2603-3 dārakau | prabrajitva sugatasya śāsane khangabhūta vanaṣaṇḍamāśṛtau | ṛddhimatta catudhyānalābhinau kāvyaśāstrakuśalausuśikṣitau | antarīkṣasadabhūmi
2603-4 kovidaute amaktagagane brajanti ca ||| te ṣa ta % tra vanaṣaṇaḍi śītale danapuṣpabharite manorame | nānapakṣidvijasaṃghasevite | anyamanya katha
2603-5 saṃprayojite ||| teśa rāja mṛgoyān aṭaṃtako śa[ptra] śrutva vanu taṃ upāgamī | dṛṣṭva pārthivata dharmabhāṇakau teṣa premaparamaṃ upasthapī tehi sarthu ka
2603-6 thamānulomiṃ kīkṛtva rāja putro niṣīdi soḥ tasya rājña valakāya ttako ṣaṣṭikoṭinayutāny upāśamī ||| teṣameku tatu dharmabhāṇako [vā]jamavra
2603-7 viścaṇohi kṣav. .. .. + + .[āca] puramaṃ sudurlabho apramantu sada bhohi rthivā ||| āyu gacchati sadā na vasthitaṃ girinadīya malilaṃ va śīgh[ra]g[ā]ṃ
children.translated_text: [Folio 2603 cont.] 'Formerly, here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, there were two diligent and excellent boys. Having gone forth in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>, like rhinoceroses (<s>khaḍga</s>) they dwelt in a forest grove. || Endowed with supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), attainers of the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), skilled in poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) and <s>śāstra</s> (treatises), well-trained — versed in the sky, earth, and atmosphere, they traveled through the unstained sky. ||| In that cool forest grove, filled with various flowers, delightful, frequented by flocks of various birds — they engaged in mutual conversation. ||| A king, while roaming on a hunt, hearing [of them], approached that forest. Having seen the two <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, the prince developed supreme affection for them. Having engaged in appropriate conversation with them, the king's son sat down. [...] of that king...

children.text:
2604-1 ga .. vyādhiśo .. [j]. .. .. .. [t]. sya va[nā]sti trāhu yatha karma bhadrakaṃ ||| dharmapālu bhava rājakuṃja rākṣimaṃ daśabalāna śāsanaṃ | kṣīṇa kāli parame
2604-2 s[u]dāruṇe dharmapakṣi sthiha rājakuṃjaraḥ || eva te bahuprakāra paṇḍitā ovadaṃti tada taṃ narādhipaṃ | sādhu ṣaṣṭinayutehi pārthivo bodhicittam udapā
2604-3 dayaṃtada || śrutva dharma tada rājakuṃjara sūtratānanakhilāna bhāṣato prītijāta sumanā udgṛko bandya pūda śirasāya prakramī ||| tasya rājña va
2604-4 havo nya bhikṣavo lābhakamā praviśaṃtu tat kulaṃ tesa dṛṣṭva cariyāṃ na tādṛśī teṣu rāja na tathā sagauravaḥ || tac ca śāsanamatītaśāstukaṃ paścimaṃ
2604-5 ca ta varṣu vartate | jaṃbudvīpisu paritta bhājanā prādurbhūta vahavo asaṃyatā utku laddha bahu tatra bhikṣivo lābhakāma upalaṃ bhadṛṣṭhikā vipranaṣṛ
2604-6 sugatasya śāsanād śrāhayaṃsu baḍātaṃ tatā tṛpaṃ || dhātayeti ubhi dharmabhāṇakau ye ucchedra pravadaṃti tīrthikāḥ dī .. [c]ārika samācapetdi tye nirvṛ
2604-7 tīya na ti kiṃvi darthikā || karma [v]arśyati vipāku naśyati skandha haṣtivi vataṃti kū[hi]kāḥ tāt k[ṣ]ipāhi viṣayātu pārthicā evam asu diru dhamu s[th]ā .y. ti |||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2604] ... disease [...] there is no refuge [...] as [virtuous] <s>karma</s> is wholesome. ||| 'Be a guardian of the <s>Dharma</s>, O royal prince! Guard the teaching of the Ten-Powered Ones (<s>Daśabala</s>)! In the terrible final age (<s>kṣīṇa-kāla</s>) when [the <s>Dharma</s>] has declined, stand firm in the camp of <s>Dharma</s>, O royal prince!' || Thus those wise ones of many kinds instructed that lord of men. The king, together with sixty <s>nayutas</s>, then generated the aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). || Having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from that royal prince who proclaimed all the <s>sūtras</s> completely, with joy arisen, cheerful and attentive, he saluted [their] feet with his head and departed with reverence. ||| To that king [came] many other <s>bhikṣus</s>, seeking gain, who entered that household. Having seen their conduct to be not like [the former's], the king was not so respectful toward them. ||

children.text:
2605-1 śrutva tesa tacana tadattare kāṃkṣa prāptu [ā] .. rā[vu]kuṃjavaraḥ ghātayiṣyi mumu [dhā]rmabhāṇakau mā upekṣa tu anarthu bheṣyati || tasya tājña anubaddha devatā p[ū]
2605-2 rvajāti sahacīrṇacārikāḥ dīrbarātru hitakāma paṇḍitā sā avaci muta rjapārthivaṃ ||| cittupādu ma janehi īdṛ[śa pā]pamitravacanena kṣatṛyāḥ
2605-3 mātva bhikṣu vidu dharmabhāṇakau pāpamitravacanena kaupāpamitra vacanena ghātaya || na tta kiṃci smirasī narādhipā yanti tehi vanaṣaṇaḍi bhāṣitaṃ ||| kṣīṇakāli param. sudāru
2605-4 ṇe dharm[a]pakṣi .thiha rājakuṃjaraḥ || rāja bhūtavacana % nena codita so na riṃcati jināna śāsanaṃ ||| tasya rājña tada bhrāta dāruṇa prātisīmiku s. tehi
2605-5 śrāhitaḥ ghātitavya ami dharmabhāṇakau ye uccheda pratipannapārthivā || dīrghacārikasamādapenti te nirvṛtīyanate kiṃci darthikāḥ || eṣa dev[i] tava bhrā
2605-6 .. pāpako jīvitena na tijā t[ū]natṛte | tasya bhikṣu durvi ghora vaidyekā te prajaṃti gagatena vidyayā || te sma śrutva [t]. va mūlamāgatā sarvi bhūt[va] tava bi
2605-7 [ṭ].. [rth]emathaḥ kṣibra .. + + + .. .o[r]. vai ..[a] kā mā ti paśca anubhāpu bheṣyati || sannahitva tada rājakuṃjaro pāpamitravacanena pras[th]itaḥ sarvasai
children.translated_text: [Folio 2605] Having heard their words, thereafter the royal prince became doubtful: 'He will have the <s>Dharma</s>-preachers killed! Do not be indifferent, for misfortune will befall [him]!' || A <s>devatā</s> (deity) attached to that king — one who had practiced together [with him] in former lives, who desired his welfare for a long night, wise — she spoke to that royal prince: ||| 'Do not generate such an intention! O <s>kṣatriya</s>, [do not heed] the words of evil friends (<s>pāpa-mitra</s>)! Knowing those <s>bhikṣus</s> to be wise <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, do not kill [them] at the words of evil friends.' || [...] 'In the terrible final age when [the <s>Dharma</s>] has declined, stand firm in the camp of <s>Dharma</s>, O royal prince!' || The king, urged by the words of truth (<s>bhūta-vacana</s>), does not abandon the [teaching of the] <s>Jinas</s> [...]

children.text: 2606-1 .. para .. .. .. p[o] .. .y. bh. [kṣu] vani taṃ upāgatoḥ || jñātt[i] ghorama[t]i dāruṇaṃ tṛpaṃ .[ā] .. y. kṣa vani tatra ye sthiṇaḥ iṭṛ varṣa tada tatra au ti .. + ///
children.translated_text: [Folio 2606] ... [...] the <s>bhikṣus</s> came to that forest. || [The king's] relatives, of fierce minds, cruel and malicious, [...] those who stood in that forest — for [many] years then there [...] ///

children.text:
2606-2 ṇaṃ nṛpaṃ nāgayakṣa tani[ḥ] tra ye sthitāḥ iṭṛvarsatada tatra [au s]irītena rāja sada penayā hato[ḥ] || .. pamitrava[c]anena paśyamāṃ kālu kṛ .v.
2606-3 da rāja dāruṇaṃ | yena krodhu kṛtu dharmabhāṇake so avīti gatu ṣaṣṭijātiyo || te pi bhikṣu bahuvopalaṃbhikāḥ ye hi śrāhitu rāja .. [.a]t[ya]yoḥ
2606-4 jātikoṭiśata te py acittiyā [v]edayiṃsu % [n]a[r]akese vedanāṃ ||| devatā yaya sarāju coditoḥ yāya rakṣitata dharmabhāṇakau .[ra]ya [nu]
2606-5 ddha yatha gaṃgavālikā dṛṣṭva pūjita caraṃta cārikāṃ ||| ṣaṣṭikoṭinayutā attanakā yehi dharmu śrutu sārdhu rājinā | yehi bodhi caracittu
2606-6 paditaṃ buddha bhūmi pṛthu lokadhātuṣu | teṣam āyu nāṇukalpakoṭiyo teṣa jñānam atulaṃ acintyaṃ [.tā] pi sa[r]vamu [s]amādhibhadrakaṃ deś. .. .[ut]u
2606-7 pada[ndr]u nirv[ṛ]tā eta śrutva vaca[n]aṃ .ir. .[t]araṃ ś[āla]śrahmaguṇajñāna saṃca[ya]ṃ | apra .atta [t]. vatrā śataṃ[tṛ]tā buddhajñānam acireṇa [la]psyathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2606 cont.] [...] the king, the <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s> who stood there [...] the king was always slain by [...] || Looking [...] with measured words, the king performed a cruel [deed]; he who made anger toward the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher (<s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>) went to <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell) for sixty births. || Those <s>bhikṣus</s> too who held many wrong views, who listened with the king [...] | for hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of births, inconceivably, they experienced sensations in the hells. ||| The deity by whom the king was urged, by whom the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher was protected — [saw] <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having seen [them], made offerings while practicing the wandering life. ||| Sixty <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of beings, by whom the <s>Dharma</s> was heard together with the king; by whom the thought of practicing toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) was generated — [they became] <s>Buddhas</s> in extensive world-systems (<s>lokadhātu</s>). Their lifespans were no fewer than <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; their knowledge was immeasurable and inconceivable; [...] all this excellent <s>samādhi</s> was taught [...] they passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || Having heard these words [...] the accumulation of virtuous qualities and knowledge — fearless [...] you will attain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge before long. ||

children.text: 2607-1 sarvalokaśaranaṃ parvāyaṇaṃ dharmava[ṣ]u jagi utsujisya .. [||]
children.translated_text: [Folio 2607] [...] the refuge of all the world, the supreme resort — having released the rain of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmavarṣa</s>) in the world [...] ||

children.text:
Samadhirajastura/Gilgit Manuscript
Chapter 22
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> / Gilgit Manuscript. Chapter 22.

children.text:
2607-1 [a]tha khalu bhagavāṃś candraprabhaṃ kumārabhūtam āmaṃtrayati sma ||| tasmāt tarhi kumāra bodhisatve
2607-2 na m[āh]āsatvena kāye nadhyavasitena jīvite nirapekṣeṇa bhavitavyaṃ | tat kasya he[t]oḥ kāyādhyavasānahe .o[he ku]ramāra akuśaladharm[ā]bh[i]saṃskāro va[t]i | [t]. .[.ā]
2607-3 t tarhi kumāra bodhisatvena mahāsatven[a] na rūpakāyatas tathāgataprajñātavyaḥ tat kasya hetoḥ dharmakāya hi buddhābhagavanto dharmakāyaprabhā[v]i .āś ca |
2607-4 na rūpakāyaprabhāvitā | tastāt tarhi kumāra bo % dhisatvena mahāsatvena tathāgatakā[y]. prāthayitukāmena | tathāgatakāyaṃ jñātukāme [n]. [y]. ṃ
2607-5 samādhir udgrahītavyaḥ paryavāptavyaḥ dhārayitavyo % vācayitavyaḥ pravartayitavya udd[e]ṣṭavyaḥ svādhyātavyaḥ bhāvayitavyaḥ bhāvanāyogam anuyuktena bha[v]i
2607-6 tavyaṃ | parebhyaś ca vista[r]eṇa saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ tatra kumāra tathāgatasya kāyaśatapuṇyanirjitayabudhyākārthanirdeśaḥ dharmanirjātaḥ ānimi .. [ḥ]
2607-7 .. .. [v]a .i [m]i ..[ā] .. .. t[ag]. ṃ bhīr[a]ḥ a .r. [m]āṇaḥ apramāṇadharmaḥ ā .. rma[tt]. [s]vabhāryaḥ sarvanimittacibhāvitaḥ ac[a]laḥ apratiṣṭhataḥ anyattākā .. +
children.translated_text: [Folio 2607 cont.] Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed prince <s>Candraprabha</s>: ||| 'Therefore, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should be without attachment to the body and without concern for life. For what reason? Because, O prince, attachment to the body is the cause of constructing unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not perceive the <s>Tathāgata</s> from the material body (<s>rūpakāya</s>). For what reason? For the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, have the <s>Dharma</s>-body (<s>Dharmakāya</s>) and are empowered by the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, not empowered by the <s>rūpakāya</s>. Therefore, O prince, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to attain the <s>Tathāgata's</s> body, who wishes to know the <s>Tathāgata's</s> body — this <s>samādhi</s> should be taken up, mastered, retained, recited, put into practice, and taught [...]'

children.text:
2608-1 .. .. .. .. [su] dvayaḥ .. .. .y. cak. [u]spa.ra[ṣ]a[m]atikrānto dharmakāyaḥ prajñātavyaḥ acintyaḥś cittabhūmivigataḥ sukhaduḥkhāciprakaṃpyaḥ sa .. prapaṃcasamatikrā
2608-2 [nt]. anirdeśyaḥ anike .. ḥ buddhajñānaṃ prārthayitukāmānāṃ | ghoṣapathasamatikrānta | sārarāgasamatikrāntaḥ abhedyo doṣapathasamatikrā[n]taḥ dṛḍho moha[pā] th.
2608-3 samatikrāntaḥ nirdiṣṭaśunyatānideśena | ajāto jātisamatikrāntaḥ anāsravaḥ vipākasamatikrāntaḥ nityocyāhā[r]eṇa vyahāraś ca śunyaḥ nir[v]iśeṣo niv[o]
2608-4 ṇe[n]a | nirvṛtaḥ śabdenaḥ śāttoghoṣeṇa | sāmā % nyaḥ saṃketena saṃketaparamārthena | paramārthobhūtavacanena | śītaloniṣparidāhaḥ animittaḥ
2608-5 [a]manyitaḥ aniṃ jitaḥ aprapaṃcitaḥ alpaśabdo nirdeś[e]na | aparyttovarṇanirdeśena | mahābhijñāparikarmanirjātaḥ as[m]ṛtitaḥ abhidūre | mahā
2608-6 bhijñā .. .. karmanirdeśena | ayam ucyate [ku]māra tathāgatakāya iti ||| atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyām imā gāthā abhāṣataḥ || ya icche lo
2608-7 kanātha[sy]a .[ā] .. ṃ jānitum īdṛśaṃ imaṃ samādhiṃ bhāvitvā kāyaṃ buddhasya jñāsyati ||| puṇyanirjātu buddhasya kāyaśuddhaḥ prasvaraḥ sameti so tta
children.translated_text: [Folio 2608] [...] having transcended the duality [...] having transcended eye-contact — the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (<s>Dharma</s>-body) is to be known as inconceivable, beyond the ground of mind, not shaken by pleasure and pain, having transcended [...] conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>), inexpressible, without [...] For those who wish to attain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge: having transcended the path of sound, having transcended passion (<s>rāga</s>), indestructible, having transcended the path of hatred (<s>doṣa</s>), firm, having transcended the path of delusion (<s>moha</s>), instructed by the teaching of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). Unborn, having transcended birth; without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), having transcended [karmic] ripening (<s>vipāka</s>). Always to be conveyed in speech, yet speech is empty; without distinction in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. | Liberated by sound, peaceful in expression. Common in convention, by the ultimate meaning (<s>paramārtha</s>) of convention. Ultimate by truthful speech. Cool, without burning, signless (<s>animitta</s>), without conceit, unconquered, beyond conceptual elaboration (<s>aprapañcita</s>), of few words [...]

children.text:
2609-1 rikṣeṇa nātvaṃ nānāsya labhyate | y[.]ādṛśā bodhibuddhasya lakṣaṇāni ca yādṛśāḥ yādṛśā lakṣaṇās tasya kāyas tasyāpi tādṛśaḥ || saṃbodhilakṣaṇakāyo buddhakṣe
2609-2 traṃ pi tādṛśaṃ | balā vimokṣā dhyānāni sarve te py ekalakṣaṇā eṣa saṃbhavu buddhānāṃ lokānāthāna īdṛśaḥ na jātu kenacic chakyaṃ paśyituṃ māṃsacakṣusāḥ bahū eve prava
2609-3 kṣayaṃti dṛṣṭo me lokanāya[ṃ]ka suvarṇavarṇaḥ kāyena sarvalokaṃ prabhāṣati ||| adhiṣṭhānena buddhānāṃm anubhāvād vikurvicai yenāsau dṛśyate kāyo lakṣaṇehi vicitrita
2609-4 ārohapariṇāhena kāyo buddhenādaśitaḥ na ca pra % māṇaṃ kāyasya labdhaṃ [t]ena acintiyaḥ yadi pramāṇaṃ labhyete ||| kāyo buddhasya e[t]tako nirviśeṣo bhavec chā
2609-5 stā devaiś [c]. ma[v]ajair api ||| samāhitasya cittasya vipaāko pi tallakṣaṇaḥ tallakṣaṇaṃ nāmarūpaṃ ca śuddhaṃ bhoti prabhāstaraṃ | na vaisa kainacijātu samādhiḥ śāntu [bhā]
2609-6 vita | t. .. h. lokanāthena kalpakoṭyo niṣevitā ||| bahubhiḥ śukladharmeś ca samādhir janito py ayaṃ samādher asya vaipulyāt kāyo mahyaṃ na dṛśyate || yasya co yā
2609-7 ..[ś]. ṃ .i .. nāma[rū]paṃ .i .[ā]d. śaṃ tiḥsvabhāvasya cittasya nāmarūpaṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ | yasya codārasaṃjñāhi nāmarūpasmi vartate visabhāgāya saṃjñā[y]a
children.translated_text: [Folio 2609] [...] by effort, neither self nor other is obtained. Whatever are the marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of the <s>Buddha's</s> awakening, and whatever marks [characterize him] — his body is of such nature. || The body characterized by perfect awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), the <s>Buddha</s>-field is also of such nature; the powers (<s>bala</s>), liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), meditations (<s>dhyāna</s>) — all are of one character. This is the origin of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Lords of the World (<s>Lokanātha</s>) — of such nature. Never can anyone see [it] with the fleshly eye. Many indeed will proclaim: 'The Lord of the World has been seen by me' — with golden-colored body he illuminates all the world. ||| By the empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, by their power and transformation (<s>vikurvita</s>), that body is seen, adorned with marks; of height and girth, the body is shown by the <s>Buddha</s>, yet no measure of the body is obtained — therefore it is inconceivable. If a measure were to be obtained, ||| the body of the <s>Buddha</s> of such extent — the Teacher would be without distinction; and the gods [...]

children.text:
2610-1 u .. .. .. .[ū]jā[yat]. [||] .. sya co mṛdukī saṃjñā nāmarūpapaṣmi vartate | agṛddhaṃ nāmarūpasmi cittaṃ bhoti prabhāsvaraṃ ||| smarāmi pūrvajā[t]īṣu asaṃkhyeyeṣu sa
2610-2 pta[su] .. [s].[o] me pāpikā sajñā naivotpannā kadācanaḥ || anāsravaṃ ca me cittaṃ kalpakoṭyo hy acintiyā karomi cārthaṃ satvānāṃ na ca me kāyu dṛśyate ||| yathā ca yasya bhāve
2610-3 hi .[i]muk[t]aṃ bhobhi mānasaṃ | na tasya tehi bhāvehi bhūyo bhoti samāgamaḥ vimuktaṃ mama vijñānaṃ sarvabhāvehi sarvaśaḥ svabhāvo jñātu vittasya bhūyo jñānaṃ pravartate |
2610-4 kṣetrakoṭīsahasrāṇi gacchanti mama nirmitāku % rvaṃti cārthaṃ satvānāṃ yatra kāyo na labhyate ||| alakṣaṇo nirnimitto yathaiva gaganaṃ tathā | kāye nirabhilapyo
2610-5 [m]e duvijñeyo nidarśana dharmakāyāmahāvīrādharmeṇo kāyunirjito | na jātu rūpakāyena śakyaṃ prajñapituṃ jino || kathā nirdeśu yasyaitaṃ śrutvā prīti [bha]vi[ṣ]ya
2610-6 ti na tasya māraḥ pāpīyān avatāraṃ labhī[ṣ]yati ||| śrutvā ca dharmaṃ gaṃbhīraṃ nāsya trāso bhaviṣyati | na cāsau jīvitārthāya buddhabodhiṃ pratikṣipet* || bhūtakoṭīsa
2610-7 hasrāṇāṃ bhūtaṃ nirdeśu jñāsyati ālokabhūto lokānāṃ yena [y]ena gamiṣyati ||| %% tatra kumāra tathāgatasya kāyaḥ ni[m]ittakarmaṇāpi na sukaraṃ jñā
children.translated_text: [Folio 2610] [...] is born. || And his perception is gentle; it operates in name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>); unattached to name-and-form, the mind becomes luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>). ||| I remember former births, in seven incalculable [<s>kalpas</s>] [...] evil perception never arose in me at any time. || And my mind is without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>) for inconceivable <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; I accomplish the benefit of beings, yet my body is not seen. ||| And just as for one whose mind is liberated from [all] existences — there is no further meeting with those existences; my consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is liberated from all existences entirely. The nature of the knowledgeable one being known, knowledge operates again. | Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of fields are traversed by my emanations (<s>nirmita</s>); they accomplish the benefit of beings where the body is not obtained. ||| Characterless, signless (<s>animitta</s>), just as space (<s>gagana</s>), so too the body — without [...]

children.translated_text: [Folio 2611] ... blue, or blue-colored, or blue in appearance, or blue in radiance; | yellow, or yellow-colored, or yellow in appearance, or yellow in radiance; | red, or red-colored, or red in appearance, or red in radiance; | white, or white-colored, or white in appearance, or white in radiance; | crimson (<s>māñjiṣṭha</s>), or crimson-colored, or crimson in appearance, or crimson in radiance; | crystal (<s>sphaṭika</s>), or crystal-colored, or crystal in appearance, or crystal in radiance; | fire-like, or fire-colored, or fire in appearance, or fire in radiance; | like clarified butter (<s>sarpirmaṇḍa</s>), or ghee-colored, or ghee in appearance, or ghee in radiance; | golden (<s>sauvarṇa</s>), or gold-colored, or gold in appearance, or gold in radiance; | lapis lazuli (<s>vaidūrya</s>), or lapis-colored, or lapis in appearance, or lapis in radiance; | lightning (<s>vidyut</s>), or lightning-colored, or lightning in appearance, or lightning in radiance; | like <s>Brahmā</s>, or <s>Brahmā</s>-colored, or <s>Brahmā</s> in appearance, or <s>Brahmā</s> in radiance; | like a <s>deva</s>, or <s>deva</s>-colored, or <s>deva</s> in appearance, or <s>deva</s> in radiance. | Thus, O prince, the <s>Tathāgata's</s> body-purity is inconceivable even by all signs — of inconceivable description. Through the perfection of the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>), it is not easy for the world with its gods to grasp the measure of the body. Apart from all [ordinary] causes, it is inconceivable, immeasurable. Then ...

children.text:
2612-1 lu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāmi gāthā abhāṣtāḥ yad rajo lokadhātūṣu pāṃsusaṃjñānidarśanaṃ | utsahradataḍāgeṣu samudreṣu ca yajjalaṃ ||| na teṣāṃ labhya
2612-2 [t]e [a]nto ettakā paramāṇavaḥ samudrā bālokoṭībhirmātuṃ śakyaṃ jalaṃ bhavet* || na tuyā lokanāthena upamā saṃprakāśitā jalaviṃdavo pramaiyās tathaiva para
2612-3 māṇavaḥ || paśyām ekasya satvāsya tato bahutarān ahaṃ adhimukticitta utpādānekakāle prajānitum* || ye mayā ātmabhāvasya bhūtāvarṇā nidarśitā sarva[s].
2612-4 tvādhimuktyās tān ateṣām upamā kṣamāḥ || nimitta % karmaṇā naiva varṇanirbhāṣa īdṛśa śakyaṃ jānitu buddhasya viśeṣo hīdṛśo mamaḥ || nimitāpagatā bu
2612-5 ddhā dharmākāyaprabhrāvitā gaṃbhīrāś cāprameyāś ca tena buddhā acittiyāḥ || acintyasya buddhasya buddhakāyo py acintiya acintiyā hi te kāyā dharmakāya
2612-6 prabhāvitā || cittenāpi na buddhānāṃ kāyaś cintayituṃ kṣamaṃ | tathā hi tasya kāyasya pramāṇaṃ nopalabhyate || pramāṇāhi te dharma kalpakoṭyo niṣeviha teno [a]
2612-7 cintiyaḥ kāyo nirvṛtto me prabhāsvaraḥ || aśrāhya | sarvasatvehi na pramāṇehi gyahyate tathā hi kāyo buddhasya na pramāṇo hy acintiṃ yaḥ || apramāṇe .i
children.translated_text: [Folio 2612] ... the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that time spoke these verses: || 'Whatever dust in world-systems, appearing as particles of sand; | whatever water in pools, ponds, lakes, and oceans — ||| the end of these cannot be found, so numerous are the atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>). The ocean-water might perhaps be measured by <s>koṭīs</s> of beings. || But no comparison has been shown by the World-Protector (<s>Lokanātha</s>); water-drops are measurable, and likewise atoms — || but I see for a single being, more numerous than those, the aspirational thought-productions at one time are to be known. || Whatever true appearances of self-existence have been shown by me — all beings' aspirations serve as similes for them. || Not by the act of signs, not by color-description of such a kind, can the distinction of the <s>Buddha</s> be known — for such is mine. || Beyond signs are the <s>Buddhas</s>, manifested through the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, profound and immeasurable — therefore <s>Buddhas</s> are inconceivable. || Of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>-body too is inconceivable; inconceivable indeed are those bodies, [manifested through] the <s>Dharmakāya</s> ...

children.text:
2613-1 dha[rm]ehi pramāṇaṃ tatra kalpitaṃ akalpitehi dhar.ehi buddho py evam akalpitaḥ || apramāṇaṃ kalpa ākhyāto apramāṇam akalpa akalpakalpā[p]agataḥs tena
2613-2 buddho acintiyaḥ || [a]pramāṇaṃ yathākāśaṃ mātuṃ śakyaṃ na kena cit* tathaiva kāyo buddha ākāśasamasādṛśaḥ || ye kāyam evaṃ jānaṃti buddhānāṃ te jinātmajā te pi
2613-3 buddhā bhaviṣyaṃti lokanāthā acintiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Folio 2613] ... by conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, a measure is established there; by unconditioned <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> too is thus unconditioned. || The immeasurable is called '<s>kalpa</s>'; the immeasurable is beyond <s>kalpa</s>. Gone beyond <s>kalpa</s> and non-<s>kalpa</s> — therefore the <s>Buddha</s> is inconceivable. || Immeasurable as space (<s>ākāśa</s>), it cannot be measured by anyone; | likewise is the body of the <s>Buddha</s>, equal to, resembling space. || Those who know the body of the <s>Buddhas</s> thus — they are sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). They too will become <s>Buddhas</s>, World-Protectors (<s>Lokanātha</s>), inconceivable. ||
